title: ‘He’s done an insane job’: Antonelli’s rivals unite in praise for F1’s youngest champion | Kimi Antonelli | The Guardian
description: Lando Norris said ‘People are not giving him enough credit’ after Kimi Antonelli sealed the world drivers’ title with a third placed finish in Mexico
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Lando Norris said ‘People are not giving him enough credit’ after Kimi Antonelli sealed the world drivers’ title with a third placed finish in Mexico
Content: Kimi Antonelli is held aloft by members from his Mercedes team after he clinched the world title.Photograph: Michael Potts/LAT ImagesView image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli is held aloft by members from his Mercedes team after he clinched the world title.Photograph: Michael Potts/LAT ImagesKimi Antonelli‘He’s done an insane job’: Antonelli’s rivals unite in praise for F1’s youngest championLando Norris: ‘People are not giving him enough credit’20-year-old sealed F1 title after finishing third in MexicoGiles Richardsat the Autódromo Hermanos RodríguezSun 1 Nov 2026 18.28 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 18.42 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFormula One’s leading drivers have been unstinting in their praise for the new champion, Kimi Antonelli, after the Italian driver took hisdebut title with third placeat the Mexican Grand Prix.Antonelli became the youngest world champion at 20 years old in Mexico, sharing a podium with race winner Max Verstappen and second-placed Lewis Hamilton. He has taken the title in only his second year in the sport after a remarkable season including nine wins.Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion with third place in Mexican GPRead more“It’s a special moment,” said Antonelli. “One that we’ll remember for ever.” While his race engineer, Peter Bonnington, suggested this may well be the first of many. “It’s a ­pleasure to be on the journey with you, but it’s just the first chapter,” he said.The defending champion, Lando Norris, led what were fulsome ­tributes to the driver who had taken his crown, emphasising that he felt Antonelli had been exceptional.“He’s done an insane job. I feel like people are not giving him enough credit for what he’s achieved this year,” said Norris. “He’s beaten the teammate that’s been in the sport for four times longer than him. Who was also very good and who took the battle to Lewis Hamilton.”His achievement was perhaps not appreciated, suggested Norris, because the Italian had been so good he had made it look easy.“[Yes] 100% he’s made it look like an easy year. They say he’s not had much competition or anything, but that’s because he slapped his competition,” he added. “I think he’s done an ­unbelievable job. Incredible, incredible job.”Verstappen and Hamilton lifted Antonelli on to their shoulders on the podium to accept the roaring approval of the crowd. The four-time and seven-time champions ­respectively were generous in their praise too.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“It’s incredible, what a season [Kimi] had,” Verstappen said. “To do that at such an age is really impressive. I’m sure this is a very emotional day with him.”Hamilton said: “A huge congratulations to Kimi and the Mercedes team, they’re all here celebrating his ­success. I’m so grateful to be in the race to witness it.”Explore more on these topicsKimi AntonelliFormula OneFormula One 2026Motor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Liverpool’s work in progress fizzles out in the face of streetwise champions | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Afternoon began with talk of a title bid, but Arsenal looked more and more comfortable as the second half wore on
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Afternoon began with talk of a title bid, but Arsenal looked more and more comfortable as the second half wore on
Content: Liverpool's Florian Wirtz tries to get around Arsenal’s Declan Rice.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersView image in fullscreenLiverpool's Florian Wirtz tries to get around Arsenal’s Declan Rice.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersLiverpoolAnalysisLiverpool’s work in progress fizzles out in the face of streetwise championsAndy Hunterat AnfieldAfternoon began with talk of a title bid, but Arsenal looked more and more comfortable as the second half wore onSun 1 Nov 2026 16.20 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 17.17 ESTShareAndoni Iraola had swatted aside any question that veered in the direction of Liverpool’s title credentials during his press conference on Friday with two simple words. “Too early,” he would respond. TheLiverpoolhead coach was dismissive in terms of the stage of the season but, as Arsenal doggedly demonstrated, too early also applies to the development of his team.Arsenal cavorted to the sound of fury at Anfield. At the final whistle Mikel Arteta leapt into the arms of the first-team coach Gabriel Heinze as he celebrated the release of his first win at Liverpool asArsenalmanager, his club’s first league victory at Anfield in 14 years and the champions moving three points clear at the top of the table. His players, tireless in the protection of Kai Havertz’s early winner, lined up to accept the acclaim from a jubilant away section. Anger filled the space around them.Arsenal hold on for first league win at Liverpool since 2012 after Kai Havertz pounces earlyRead moreFrom Virgil van Dijk collecting a post-match booking for sarcastically applauding the referee, Andy Madley, to the jeers of the home crowd, enraged by the match officials and most of all by Arsenal’s streetwise tactics/shithousery (delete as appropriate), this was an infuriating evening for a team that had arrived with momentum and amid talk of a potential title challenge. There was only applause for Liverpool’s players as they left the pitch in recognition of their effort and misfortune.The hosts should have had a penalty for Jurriën Timber tugging Alexander Isak’s shirt and preventing him from connecting with a Bradley Barcola cross. Florian Wirtz struck the crossbar during Liverpool’s brightest spell and Alexis Mac Allister squandered a free header from 10 yards out. But as the second half ticked by and Arsenal absorbed the pressure, with Gabriel Magalhães and Declan Rice to the fore, belief in Liverpool’s powers of recovery faded.There was no clearer sign of an expensively assembled team running out of ideas than Van Dijk operating as a makeshift centre‑forward in the final exchanges. He had Isak, Barcola and the substitutes Lewis Koumas, Victor Muñoz and Rio Ngumoha in support. Ngumoha had an impact but, ultimately, Liverpool’s varied forward line did not. For the first time in 16 years Liverpool failed to register a shot on target in a Premier League game.Iraola’s complaint about Liverpool’s two defeats this season both turning on contentious refereeing decisions was valid. But he ended that particular discussion with a telling point. “I think it’s a penalty but we need to think about what we can improve to be on the right side of these big games,” Iraola admitted.View image in fullscreenTrey Nyoni impressed after Andoni Iraola handed him a first Premier League start.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAAnother slow start cost Liverpool but they also lacked the penetration and the defensive might that underpinned Arsenal’s win. That will come in time under Iraola. In the meantime, there will be harsh lessons to occasionally absorb.The Liverpool head coach again showed he is prepared to trust and reward young talent by handing a first start in the Premier League to Trey Nyoni. It was a bold call from Iraola, with Ryan Gravenberch dropped to the bench alongside the fit-again Dominik Szoboszlai to accommodate the 19-year-old, but one based on merit. Nyoni impressed Iraola from the moment he walked into the club this summer and stepped up a level on Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US. The debut had been coming, and there was added weight to the vote of confidence that it should come against such formidable opposition.Nyoni made his presence felt immediately. One reservation over the midfielder’s inclusion against a midfield of Rice, Bruno Guimarães and Martin Ødegaard was whether he had the physicality to compete. After merely 49 seconds he left Ødegaard in a heap to concede the game’s first free-kick. In the 10th minute he caught Havertz’s ankle with a late challenge and was perhaps fortunate to avoid the game’s first booking.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion‘We have to tell them to go down’: Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial for LiverpoolRead moreNyoni’s timing was more accurate, his speed and strength clear, when beating Ødegaard convincingly in a 50‑50 challenge as they closed in on a David Raya throw. Arsenal rightly survived a video assistant referee’s check for a penalty against Christos Tzolis in the spell of pressure that followed Nyoni’s intervention.The youngster’s composure on the ball and intelligent reading of the game were the most encouraging aspects of his full league debut. What worked against Nyoni, however, was Liverpool’s need to chase the game from as early as the 16th minute. Iraola needed attacking aggression and chaos in the final third more than the teenager’s defensive protection and patient buildup play. It was a reflection of the circumstances, not Nyoni’s own contribution, when he was replaced by Szoboszlai in the 59th minute.There was chaos but no clarity to Liverpool’s performance in the final third, however. Despite the anguish over the antics of Gabriel, Havertz and the performance of Madley, there was a gap between the champions and potential contenders. Too early, as Iraola would say. But give it time.Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolArsenalanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Ciara Mageean, European 1500m gold medallist with Ireland, dies aged 34 | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Ireland’s European 1500 metres gold medallist Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Ireland’s European 1500 metres gold medallist Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34
Content: Ciara Mageean, pictured in Glasgow in 2019, competed at the 2016 and 2020 Olympic Games and was ‘respected and loved by many people’.Photograph: Jane Barlow/PAView image in fullscreenCiara Mageean, pictured in Glasgow in 2019, competed at the 2016 and 2020 Olympic Games and was ‘respected and loved by many people’.Photograph: Jane Barlow/PAAthleticsCiara Mageean, European 1500m gold medallist with Ireland, dies aged 34Mageean won 2024 European 1500m title in RomeAthlete described as ‘an inspiration to so many’Press AssociationSun 1 Nov 2026 07.31 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 17.40 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Irish middle-distance runner Ciara Mageean, who won European gold and competed at two Olympic Games, has died aged 34, her family have announced.The athlete, from Portaferry in Northern Ireland, died at 6.30am on Sunday. In a post on social media, her family said she was surrounded by her loved ones, adding: “A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed.”Mageean was one of the most high‑profile athletes in Ireland, specialising in the 1500m event. She represented Ireland at the 2016 Rio Olympics and 2020 Tokyo Games, as well as holding a slew of Irish records.She became the first individual Irish European champion since Sonia O’Sullivan when she won gold at the 2024 championships in Rome. Mageean was unable to compete at the 2024 Olympics because of an achilles injury. The following year, she announced she had been diagnosed with cancer. She went on to marry her partner, Thomas Moran, in October only weeks before her death.Micheál Martin, the Taoiseach, said he was deeply saddened at her passing. “My heartfelt sympathies go to her husband Thomas, all her family and friends,” he said. The Tánaiste, Simon Harris, described the news as heartbreaking. He said: “She was a European champion, two-time Olympian, a proud Irish athlete and an extraordinary person.”Northern Ireland’s first minister, Michelle O’Neill, said Mageean demonstrated “extraordinary talent, determination and dedication”, adding: “I am deeply saddened to hear of the passing of Ciara Mageean, and I want to extend my heartfelt condolences to her husband Tommy, her parents, family, friends and everyone who loved her.“Ciara’s achievements in athletics brought immense pride to her local community and to people right across Ireland. From representing Ireland at two Olympic Games to winning European championship gold in Rome in 2024, Ciara demonstrated extraordinary talent, determination and dedication.View image in fullscreenCiara Mageean (left) competing for Northern Ireland at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA“However, beyond the medals, records and sporting accolades, Ciara will be remembered for her warmth, courage and tremendous strength of character. Throughout her illness, she showed a remarkable spirit and an incredible ability to find hope and joy in life, even in the most difficult circumstances. Her courage touched countless people and will leave a lasting legacy.“For a community like Portaferry, this loss will be deeply felt. Ciara was one of our own, and the pride she brought to her community and beyond will never be forgotten. At this incredibly difficult time, I hope her family and loved ones can take some comfort from knowing just how deeply she was admired, respected and loved by so many people.”The deputy first minister, Emma Little-Pengelly, said: “I am so sorry to hear of the death of Ciara Mageean, at the age of 34 years. An outstanding athlete and ambassador for her sport, Ciara was born in Portaferry, County Down, and represented Northern Ireland and predominantly Ireland on the world stage.“Ciara had outstanding success, and was an inspiration to many. She spoke with such honesty and bravery about the health battles she subsequently faced. I know so many from right across Northern Ireland were deeply proud and inspired by Ciara. My deepest condolences to her family, teammates and friends, and her husband to whom she had so recently married.”Explore more on these topicsAthleticsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Borthwick urges England players to improve discipline at Nations Championship | England rugby union team | The Guardian
description: The coach highlighted the need to adjust to refereeing interpretations, while Ellis Genge called the timing of ‘hip-drop’ tackle law change ‘beserk’
Author: Robert Kitson
Headline: The coach highlighted the need to adjust to refereeing interpretations, while Ellis Genge called the timing of ‘hip-drop’ tackle law change ‘beserk’
Content: England’s disciplinary record in 2026 has not been good so far with 14 yellow cards and one red.Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEngland’s disciplinary record in 2026 has not been good so far with 14 yellow cards and one red.Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty ImagesEngland rugby union teamBorthwick urges England players to improve discipline at Nations Championship‘A big breakdown challenge is coming,’ warns head coachGenge calls timing of ‘hip-drop’ tackle law change ‘beserk’Robert KitsonSun 1 Nov 2026 11.00 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 14.16 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSteve Borthwick is urging his England players to act smarter and recognise the vital importance of keeping 15 players on the field before a pivotal month for the national team. Borthwick’s side have been shown 14 yellow cards and one red in 2026 to date and, partly as a consequence, have lost five of their past seven Tests.Borthwick is also concerned that different refereeing interpretations in the domestic Prem are not helping England at international level, with the latest complication being a mid‑season law change preventing so-called “hip-drop” tackles. His experienced prop Ellis Genge has called the timing of the alteration “berserk” but also fully accepts England must improve their disciplinary record in their autumnNations Championshipfixtures.The Breakdown | England need to unearth World Cup core despite derby friction and injury chaosRead moreAll national coaches were invited to a meeting with officials on Sunday to discover how exactly the November games will be refereed but Borthwick has already identified two key areas where England need to be watchful. “From my point of view there are some aspects we need to bridge from club rugby to Test rugby,” he said.“One would be the contact area. I think that was probably exemplified by last month’s Champions Cup round where the English clubs lost more ball at the breakdown than any other nation and won less back. That’s telling us straight away there’s a situation we need to bridge. When you look at the teams we are playing against in the next few weeks there is a big breakdown challenge coming.”Borthwick is also highlighting defensive steel – “We need to ensure we make it very, very difficult for the opposition to score” – which the head coach also believes is not being aided by the four-try bonus-point system in the Prem. He would prefer the adoption of the French system where teams must score three tries more than their opponents to secure an extra point.“My view on the bonus-point structure is that it shouldn’t be the way it is,” he said. “I think the evidence says it should follow the Top 14, which makes defence important right until the 80th minute. I think that’s not necessarily always the case [in the Prem]. Nobody’s to blame or at fault, that’s just the way it’s structured.”View image in fullscreenEllis Genge (third right) has been critical of the mid-season law change regarding ‘hip-drop’ tackles in the Prem.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianAs for his side’s tactical discipline, Borthwick has also changed his tune since July when he dubbed the media “the negativity committee” after the31-24 win against Argentinain Santiago del Estero when he was asked about England’s concession of four yellow cards in the second half. “The best players are smart and the best players adjust,” said Borthwick, who invited the referee Christophe Ridley to address his players last week.“It’s pretty obvious there have been times over the last six to eight months when we haven’t dealt with moments the way we want to. At the 2023 World Cup this team had excellent habits … really it’s been the autumn of 2025 into this year’s Six Nations that cost us.“Quite frankly we spend too much time defending. The way the interpretations are right now there is likely to be a decision that goes against you which gives an entry into the 22. As soon as you are there, we can all see the number of cards. We spent too much time there … we want to get the ball back faster.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOn the subject of outlawed “hip-drop” tackles, when players try to bring down an opponent from behind by sliding in on their knees and dropping their weight on to the opponent’s lower limbs, Borthwick also wants his players to learn fast before the game against Australia on Sunday. “I don’t think we can argue against anything that protects the players who play this intense game. What we’ve got to be is the quickest team to adjust.”Genge believes the sport as a whole needs to stop altering its regulations for the sake of the players and new fans. “I think the fact our game after all this time still changes rules year to year is berserk, particularly when we’re speaking about making it palatable for new people to come in. I think it’s mental but I assume they’re trying to refine it for the best.”England, meanwhile, have fresh injury concerns at scrum-half with Northampton’s Alex Mitchell (hamstring) and the uncapped Archie McParland (calf) struggling. With the fly-halfFin Smith (calf) already in a race against time to face the Wallabies, the management may have to start Leicester’s Jack van Poortvliet at nine, potentially with either Marcus Smith or George Ford outside him.Explore more on these topicsEngland rugby union teamSteve BorthwickNations ChampionshipRugby unionPrem RugbynewsShareReuse this content

title: Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: The WSL champions Manchester City were fortunate to leave London City Lionesses with three points after Lauren Hemp secured a 2-1 win
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: The WSL champions Manchester City were fortunate to leave London City Lionesses with three points after Lauren Hemp secured a 2-1 win
Content: Lauren Hemp (left) and Khadija Shaw react after Manchester City take a 2-1 lead.Photograph: Dave Shopland/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenLauren Hemp (left) and Khadija Shaw react after Manchester City take a 2-1 lead.Photograph: Dave Shopland/ShutterstockWomen's Super LeagueHemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thrillerSuzanne WrackSun 1 Nov 2026 09.13 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 12.54 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGoals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp helped Manchester City to escape from Bromley with three points after a thrilling encounter withLondon City Lionesses. It was a statement performance from the home team, despite the defeat delivering a blow to any title ambitions they may have been quietly holding on to before kick-off.The gap between the hosts and the champions is now six points, after Hemp restored City’s lead following Jana Fernández’s equaliser. But that London City had even played their way into conversations about this season’s title contenders in their second season has been impressive.Russo spares Arsenal blushes but latest setback increases pressure on SlegersRead moreAndrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City manager, praised the ability of his team to win in different ways as needed, after three games in eight days. “We said afterwards, the players should be so proud of what they put into this game,” he said.“We’ve learned we’re a great team who can keep the ball for 75% of the game and win that way, or we can win like this. That quality to win in different ways is good to have, but the players also have to adapt to that and feel it’s OK to not have the ball all the time, take pride in defending and only having three or four chances but finishing off those chances.”Before kick-off, cameras showed London City’s superstar summer signing Alexia Putellas opening the boot of her car and taking out a heavy leather-clad square item, her third Ballon d’Or safely encased inside. The Spain midfielder did not present her trophy to fans in the stands before kick-off, instead choosing to put it on display so supporters could queue to have their photo taken with it.The only nod to the player’s stunning individual year, in which she won the quadruple with Barcelona before joining London City, was on her feet, the geometric gold on her custom Ballon d’Or-themed boots glinting on their first outing.There have been jokes aplenty about the unlikelihood of the world’s premier individual award heading to its new Bromley home. To reach the stadium from Hayes Lane, you pass a field of horses on your left. London City Lionesses are not Barcelona, and they have become the home of the Ballon d’Or winner by default rather than being the key component of that individual success.Except, based on the season London City are having and the ruthless ambitions of the owner, Michelle Kang, the idea that the club could produce a season that delivers them collective success and individual success off the back of it feels less distant than it did just a few short months ago.Against the champions, London City more than held their own, the opportunity to move level on points with their opponents and league leaders Chelsea an inviting incentive. Their threat was evident within 30 seconds, when the Manchester City defender Rebecca Knaak was forced to turn Lucía Corrales’s cross wide of the far post just ahead of a waiting Isobel Goodwin.Neither team has impressed defensively this season, each only managing to keep one clean sheet in the Women’s Super League, and it made for a thrilling encounter, the high lines and aggressiveness of both attacks delivering a showstopper.Making her first WSL start for the home team, with Elene Lete hitherto preferred, Mary Earps made a huge statement with an impressive double save from a Knaak header to keep the game goalless going into the break.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenMary Earps dives at the feet of Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesCity broke the deadlock despite London City dominating and it was their most influential player who delivered. Hemp flicked the ball into the run of Shaw and with her first touch, she took it past Earps before she switched the ball on to her right foot and fired in to become just the third player to score in eight consecutive WSL starts.A deserved equaliser arrived in the 72nd minute, when Fernández was at the near post to meet a corner and her assured header sent the ball looping in at the back post.The celebrations were emphatic but they were short-lived. This is a new, more resilient Manchester City, one that survived various scares last term to secure a second WSL title, and they re-established their lead two minutes later, when Hemp stretched out a leg to poke in Mary Fowler’s cross from the right to secure the win.That London City could feel aggrieved at having not taken something from the game was a testament to their performance and how quickly progress is being made. The home team had 23 shots to City’s seven and 52 touches in the opposition box to City’s 13, but critically the visiting team were clinical when it mattered. Converting two of their three efforts on target and showing the edge needed to battle at the top.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueLondon City LionessesManchester City WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: GB’s Harriet Dart wins maiden WTA title at 30 with Guangzhou Open triumph | Tennis | The Guardian
description: Harriet Dart, having reached her first WTA final as a qualifier, beat the 18-year-old Austrian Lilli Tagger 4-6, 6-3, 6-4
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Harriet Dart, having reached her first WTA final as a qualifier, beat the 18-year-old Austrian Lilli Tagger 4-6, 6-3, 6-4
Content: Harriet Dart celebrates with her trophy after her three-set defeat of Lilli Tagger in the Guangzhou Open final.Photograph: APView image in fullscreenHarriet Dart celebrates with her trophy after her three-set defeat of Lilli Tagger in the Guangzhou Open final.Photograph: APTennisGB’s Harriet Dart wins maiden WTA title at 30 with Guangzhou Open triumphBriton beats 18-year-old Austrian Lilli Tagger 4-6, 6-3, 6-4Dart, a qualifier, was competing in her first WTA finalPress AssociationSun 1 Nov 2026 06.20 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 17.55 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHarriet Dart won her first WTA title after the Briton came from a set down to defeat Lilli Tagger in the final of the Guangzhou Open in China.Dart, who saved three match points in her semi-final against Sun Xinran to reach her first tour‑level final, edged a thrilling match against the 18‑year‑old Austrian 4-6, 6-3, 6-4.The British No 5, a qualifier for the tournament, dropped serve in the opening game and had to save a break point in her next service game before finally getting on the board against the fourth seed. The 30‑year‑old from Hampstead broke back for 4-4 but Tagger, who won the 2025 junior French Open, hit straight back before wrapping up the first set.View image in fullscreenA tearful Harriet Dart covers her eyes after beating Lilli Tagger of Austria in the Guangzhou Open final.Photograph: APDart took the first break point of the second set for 5-3 on her way to levelling the match.In a tense deciding set, a run of five consecutive breaks of serve ended when a gutsy Dart saved two break points to hold for 5-3. In the next game she brought up two champion­ship points, but a big serve from ­Tagger saved the first before Dart hit a mid‑court forehand into the net on the second.However, Dart wiped that miss from her mind to serve out the match to 15, falling on her back in delight when victory was sealed with an unreturned serve.Dart, who has been working with the former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli, said on court: “I’ll try not to get too emotional. A big thank you to my team this week. It’s ­amazing to play in front of such a big crowd. It’s been so much fun here and I really appreciate it and hope to be back next year.“This week shows that even when I’m down – and people think I’m down and out – I’m still able to overcome it. Today was a really tough match. I have no doubt Lilli will go on and win multiple titles. To come through a week like this means a lot.”Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Dart’s victory will lift her back into the top 100 and secures direct entry into the Australian Open in January. The British player has won 19 of her 24 tour-level matches on the hard courts since Wimbledon, taking her overall record on the tour this season to 23 victories from 34 matches – the highest winning percentage of her career.Explore more on these topicsTennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: NFL roundup: Cowboys and Chiefs suffer late collapses; Lamar Jackson’s season could be over | NFL | The Guardian
description: Arizona roared back to beat Dallas in overtime thanks to Gardner Minshew’s heroics while Baltimore suffered a serious injury blow
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Arizona roared back to beat Dallas in overtime thanks to Gardner Minshew’s heroics while Baltimore suffered a serious injury blow
Content: Gardner Minshew celebrates his team’s win over the Cowboys.Photograph: Stacy Revere/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenGardner Minshew celebrates his team’s win over the Cowboys.Photograph: Stacy Revere/Getty ImagesNFLNFL roundup: Cowboys and Chiefs suffer late collapses; Lamar Jackson’s season could be overGardner Minshew’s heroics inspire ArizonaJackson needs surgery on injured thumbAgenciesSun 1 Nov 2026 16.56 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 20.11 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleArizona Cardinals 33–30 Dallas Cowboys (OT)Chad Ryland kicked a winning 42-yard field goal in overtime after missing a PAT that would have won the game with six seconds left in regulation, and the Arizona Cardinals rallied for a wild victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. The Cardinals beat Dallas for the fifth consecutive time and improved to 5-0 at AT+T Stadium, the home of the Cowboys that opened in 2009.This was by far the most crushing of those for the Cowboys (3-5), who didn’t trail until the final kick and led by two touchdowns early in the fourth quarter. Arizona (3-5) were still in the game because Tyler Allgeier had a 63-yard touchdown run, a career long, followed by a 50-yarder to set up his second touchdown on a five-yard catch, all in the second half. He had 191 scrimmage yards (147 yards rushing, 44 receiving), all but seven coming after half-time.The Dallas defense was having its best showing of the season before buckling in the last 16 minutes, particularly the final minute. The Cardinals went 80 yards in eight plays after taking over with 1:05 left in regulation, tying the score at 30-30 on Gardner Minshew’s 14-yard touchdown to Michael Wilson with six seconds to go. Ryland was wide left on the PAT kick after making his previous 58.Kansas City Chiefs 24-28 Denver BroncosMalcolm Roach sacked Patrick Mahomes on the final play, securing Denver’s comeback win over Kansas City. The victory puts the Broncos (6-2) in first place in the AFC West. Denver trailed 24-13 in the third quarter, but Bo Nix threw a 2-yard TD pass and a twp-point conversion to close the gap. After Kansas City’s Harrison Butker missed a crucial field goal, Denver quickly took the lead. Mahomes had a chance to respond for the Chiefs (5-2) but was stopped at the goalline in the final seconds. Nix finished with 222 yards and two touchdowns, while Mahomes had 320 yards and three touchdowns.Baltimore Ravens 10-36 Buffalo BillsJosh Allen set the franchise record for career touchdown passes and also rushed for a score and the Buffalo Bills took advantage of multiple ⁠Baltimore quarterback injuries to notch victory over the Ravens. The Ravens (4-4) lost quarterbacks Lamar Jackson (right thumb) and Tyler “Snoop” ​Huntley (right toe) in the first half while dropping ‌their third straight game. Jackson missed ‌the previous three games with a left ankle injury. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said after the game that Jackson needs surgery on the injured thumb and his season could be over. “That’ll be a surgery deal. He’ll go to [injured reserve],” Minter said. “That’s a tough deal.” Asked if Jackson’s season was over, Minter replied: ““Potentially, but we’ll see where it’s at.”Allen’s 11-yard scoring pass to DJ Moore with 12:18 left in the ⁠game was the 259th of ⁠his career, a ​mark that includes postseason play. The previous record was held by Hall of Famer Jim Kelly, who threw 237 in the regular season and 21 in ⁠the postseason for the Bills. Allen later threw a second touchdown pass and was 21-of-34 passing for 289 yards and one interception as Buffalo (6-1) won their third straight game. James Cook III ⁠rushed for 80 yards and a touchdown for Buffalo.Minnesota Vikings 15–19 Detroit LionsJared Goff threw a go-ahead, seven-yard touchdown pass to Jameson Williams with 4:35 left and the Detroit Lions beat the Minnesota Vikings, handing the NFL’s last undefeated team their first loss. The Lions (5-2) have won three straight, including their first two division games in the tight NFC North. The Vikings (6-1) had a chance to stay unbeaten, but the league’s stingiest defense couldn’t hold on to a late lead, and they lost for the first time since 30 November 2025. The Lions lost All-Pro linebacker to a neck injury and he was taken to hospital. Campbell was placed on a backboard and carted off the field early in the fourth quarter. Lions coach Dan Campbell said he did not have any additional information after the game. “We’re thinking about him,” he said.Atlanta Falcons 0-16 Tampa Bay BuccaneersBaker Mayfield didn’t complete a pass but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell’s rushing on a wet, sloppy field. The Buccaneers set a team record for yards rushing in a game with 324, and became the first team to have zero completions since Buffalo in September 1974. Irving ran for 170 yards and a touchdown on 27 carries, Gainwell ran for 140 on 25 carries and Chase McLaughlin kicked three field goals to stay perfect this season. Mayfield was 0 for 3 passing. Atlanta’s Michael Penix Jr threw four interceptions. Both teams are 3-5.Los Angeles Chargers 9–24 Los Angeles RamsThe Los Angeles Rams overcame a slow start for a victory over the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Matthew Stafford passed for 157 yards and a touchdown, Blake Corum and Kyren Williams rushed for scores, and Puka Nacua had 11 catches for 80 yards and a TD. The Rams (4-4) have won back-to-back games for the first time this season after rallying past their SoFi Stadium roommates. Justin Herbert passed for 257 yards and threw two interceptions for the 0-7 Chargers, who returned from their bye week and extended their worst start to a season since 2000.Cleveland Browns 6–27 Pittsburgh SteelersJaylen Warren tied a career high with 143 rushing yards and a touchdown on his 28th birthday to lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to victory over the Cleveland Browns. The Steelers moved into first place all alone at 6-2 after beating the Browns at home for the 23rd straight time in the regular season, tying an NFL record. The Steelers dominated the line of scrimmage, rushing for 200 yards, including 160 in the first half alone. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson spent most of the day under heavy pressure. The Steelers sacked Watson eight times to drop the Browns to 5-3.Tennessee Titans 36–43 Cincinnati Bengals (OT)Joe Burrow threw five touchdown passes in regulation and then scrambled untouched for a nine-yard score in overtime as the Cincinnati Bengals rallied for a thrilling victory over the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati have won three straight and are 5-2 for the first time since the 2021 season, when they reached the Super Bowl. The Bengals got the ball first in OT and went 70 yards in five plays. Tennessee took over but could not get a first down. Cam Ward had the first 300-yard passing game of his two-year career but threw incomplete on fourth down to end the contest. The Titans (1-7) took an early 13-0 lead, and the fourth quarter featured three lead changes and a tie.New England Patriots 24–19 Miami DolphinsDrake Maye threw two touchdown passes and rushed for a score as the New England Patriots came back to beat the Miami Dolphins (1-6). With star receiver AJ Brown inactive because of lingering injuries, Maye completed 16 of 20 passes for 199 yards as the Patriots (5-3) rallied from a 10-point halftime deficit to take a 17-13 lead entering the fourth, then held on after a late Miami rally. DeMario Douglas caught a pass and weaved through the Dolphins secondary for a 48-yard touchdown catch that put the Patriots up two scores early in the fourth.Indianapolis Colts 7–42 Jacksonville JaguarsTrevor Lawrence threw three touchdown passes, including one to the previously benched receiver Brian Thomas Jr, and the Jacksonville Jaguars dominated the Indianapolis Colts in the rain to extend their home winning streak in the series to 12. Lawrence also connected with Bhayshul Tuten in the third quarter and rookie Nate Boerkircher on a 31-yarder in an opening half filled with big plays for the 5-2 Jaguars. It came five days after the 2-6 Colts traded two of their best players, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and longtime guard Quenton Nelson, to kickstart a rebuilding effort.Las Vegas Raiders 38–33 New York JetsKirk Cousins threw two of his three touchdown passes in the second half and ran for another score to lead the ⁠Las Vegas Raiders to a comeback victory over the New York Jets. Cousins completed 19 ⁠of 26 passes for ⁠247 yards ​as the Raiders (4-4) stopped a four-game skid, erasing a pair of nine-point deficits by scoring 17 of the game’s final 20 points. Las ⁠Vegas ended a streak of 12 straight losses when trailing at half-time. The Jets (2-6) scored on their first six possessions but frequently stalled in the red zoneExplore more on these topicsNFLUS sportsBaltimore RavensnewsShareReuse this content

title: Tonga’s gripping win over Samoa a victory for Pasifika pride at Rugby League World Cup | Rugby League World Cup | The Guardian
description: Tonga’s defeat of Samoa in a pulsating match showcased the best of Pasifika rugby league though it was not by enough to save England from an early World Cup exit
Author: Gavin Willacy
Headline: Tonga’s defeat of Samoa in a pulsating match showcased the best of Pasifika rugby league though it was not by enough to save England from an early World Cup exit
Content: Jojo Fifita of Tonga celebrates after scoring a try against Samoa in a pulsating match.Photograph: Cameron Spencer/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJojo Fifita of Tonga celebrates after scoring a try against Samoa in a pulsating match.Photograph: Cameron Spencer/Getty ImagesRugby League World CupTonga’s gripping win over Samoa a victory for Pasifika pride at Rugby League World CupTonga defeat Samoa 20-18 in raucous atmosphereEngland exit tournament on points differenceGavin Willacyat CommBank StadiumSun 1 Nov 2026 06.05 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 18.27 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSometimes sport does live up to the hype. Any suggestion that there was little riding on this result was evidently nonsense, when weeks of anticipation evolved into a mass display of national pride, the desire to get one over on their Pasifika cousins far greater than wanting to avoid Australia in the semi-finals. Tonga and Samoa flags had flown from cars for several days across the eastern seaboard and five hours before kick-off the streets of Parramatta were throng with huge groups of both nationalities celebrating their cultural bond.Both teams were basically through to the final four, yet still produced an exhilarating derby that confirmed England’s exit from theRugby League World Cupon points difference. Fans who’d paid sums previously unheard of for international rugby league tickets on the black market and resale sites will consider it money well spent. Those who got theirs for $20 will consider it the buy of the year.Any game would struggle to live up to the pre-match activities that had the CommBank crowd at fever pitch. But Brian To’o’s electrifying early darts and bullocking runs by Tongan props Jason Taumalolo and Addin Fonua-Blake laid platforms for both sides to attack. From there, Samoa looked uncertain in good ball situations while Tonga consistently threatened, Tolutau Koula denied a try by the video referee as the returning Isaiya Katoa linking their attacks beautifully from halfback. But it would take a magnificent side-stepping solo run by Robert Toia down the right centre channel to open the scoring at the predominantly Tongan end 27 minutes in.Captain Jarome Luai tried to fire Samoa up with a ferocious hit on Spencer Leniu and it was his booming kick that was fumbled by Tonga, Stephen Crichton manufacturing something from nothing to send Brian To’o in for their first points. Toia got the first after the break, finishing a fluid move on the left, Katoa extending the lead to 14-4. Samoa had to strike next and did with a repeat move, Luai’s high kick to the right, a fumble and a wonderful overhead pass, this time by Chanel Harris-Tavita, laid up To’o for his second. Harris-Tavita pulled a hamstring hitting a post with the conversion attempt and hobbled away, his World Cup done. Samoa weren’t going quietly, though. Lehi Hopoate knocked the ball out of Salesi Foketi’s hands as he plunged over the line, the teams exchanging massive hits as the fans swapped hymns.Samoa, finalists four years ago, were not fading away. Slick handling down the left sent in Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow untouched, but replacement kicker Ronald Volkman made it zero from three for Samoa from the tee and they still trailed. He made up for it a couple of minutes later, bouncing off tackles to complete a dazzling team move and finally put Samoa ahead. His kick made it 18-14 with 10 minutes to play.View image in fullscreenTonga’s Jojo Fifita attempts to score a try against Samoa.Photograph: Mark Metcalfe/Getty ImagesLuai’s attempts to keep his team calm fell on ears deafened by the racket from the frenzied stands. Instead, Addin Fonua-Blake blasted through tired tacklers to level and Katoa’s conversion put Tonga back in front. There were times when Tonga’s veteran forwards Tyson Frizell – who’d previously played in World Cups for Wales and Australia – and captain Taumalolo looked exhausted but they went to the well one more time to produce heroic defensive efforts. And when Sua Fa’alogo’s toe touched the touchline and his try was ruled out two minutes from time, Samoa’s race was run. They will face the Kangaroos across Sydney on Sunday, while Tonga take on the Kiwis in Newcastle in Saturday’s semi-final.Twenty years ago last week, Tonga beat Samoa in front of a couple of thousand neutrals in Leeds. It’s now the biggest fixture in international rugby league, with a ground record of 29,411 rejoicing in the occasion. World Cup organisers, the Australia Rugby League Commission, will have been thrilled with the sell-out event, thousands of Lebanese adding to the atmosphere. Their extraordinary 24-20 golden point win over France in the second game of a triple-header being the game of the tournament until this one, both proving dead rubbers can be corkers. Somehow the ARLC has found itself both host and promoter of the world’s biggest Pasifika party. Peter V’landys and Co will now be figuring out how to put on a repeat event every year.Explore more on these topicsRugby League World CupTongarugbyleagueteamSamoa rugby league teamRugby League World Cup 2026England rugby league teamRugby leaguenewsShareReuse this content

Author: Guardian staff reporter

title: Police detain 325 people at pro-Palestine Action protest at US embassy in London | Palestine Action | The Guardian
description: Arrests come ahead of Wednesday’s supreme court challenge to the ban on the direct action group
Author: Haroon Siddique
Headline: Arrests come ahead of Wednesday’s supreme court challenge to the ban on the direct action group
Content: Police and protesters at Saturday’s Defend Our Juries demonstration in London in support of Palestine Action.Photograph: Martin Pope/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenPolice and protesters at Saturday’s Defend Our Juries demonstration in London in support of Palestine Action.Photograph: Martin Pope/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockPalestine ActionPolice detain 325 people at pro-Palestine Action protest at US embassy in LondonArrests come ahead of Wednesday’s supreme court challenge to the ban on the direct action groupHaroon SiddiqueLegal affairs correspondentSun 1 Nov 2026 12.29 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 12.31 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePolice have said they arrested 325 people on Saturday ata demonstration outside the US embassy in Londonagainst the proscription of Palestine Action.In updated arrest figures released on Sunday, the Metropolitan police said 320 people were detained outside the building in Battersea, south London, for allegedly expressing support for an organisation banned under the Terrorism Act.The arrests came ahead of Wednesday’ssupreme court challengeto the ban on Palestine Action – the first direct action group to be proscribed under the Terrorism Act – which came into effect on 5 July last year.Defend Our Juries, which has organised the mass civil disobedience campaign against proscription, said Saturday’s detentions took the total number of people arrested for allegedly supportingPalestine Actionsince the ban to 4,200. Most arrests have been for holding placards reading “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action.”The overall number of detentions will probably feature in the hearing before the UK’s highest court, which was granted on the basis that it was arguable that the ban represents a disproportionate interference with the rights of freedom of speech and protest.View image in fullscreenHundreds of protesters hold signs outside the US embassy in London on Saturday.Photograph: Martin Pope/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockHowever, neither the high court,which ruled that the ban was unlawful, nor the court of appeal,which overturned the high court’s decision, gave much weight to the fate of the placard-holders.About 2,500 of those arrested for alleged support ofPalestineAction have been charged under the Terrorism Act but all trials have been postponed pending a definitive decision on whether or not the ban was lawful.Saturday’s demonstrations – there was also a vigil in Edinburgh, althoughPoliceScotland made no arrests – were the largest, against the ban, of Andy Burnham’s premiership.In September, when quizzed by LBC radio’s Andrew Marr about the “elderly people, vicars and grannies” who have been arrested for holding placards allegedly supporting Palestine Action, the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, said: “I don’t think anyone’s intent was to have those people criminalised. But obviously the supreme court has got to look at this issue and obviously it’s something we keep looking at as a government.”The following week, in an interview with The Rest is Politics podcast, Shabana Mahmood said it had been “very uncomfortable” to see some protesters arrested for alleged support of Palestine Action. Mahmood, the home secretary, nevertheless defended the ban.The supreme court hearing will conclude on Thursday, with judgment reserved until a later date.Explore more on these topicsPalestine ActionPalestineProtestActivismPolicenewsShareReuse this content

title: Juan Atkins, pioneer of Detroit techno sound, dies aged 64 | Dance music | The Guardian
description: US artist known as Model 500 and as one half of the duo Cybotron had huge influence on dance music worldwide
Author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
Headline: US artist known as Model 500 and as one half of the duo Cybotron had huge influence on dance music worldwide
Content: Juan Atkins was the first person to use the term ‘techno’ to describe the hard electronic style he pioneered in Detroit.Photograph: Andre BritoView image in fullscreenJuan Atkins was the first person to use the term ‘techno’ to describe the hard electronic style he pioneered in Detroit.Photograph: Andre BritoDance musicJuan Atkins, pioneer of Detroit techno sound, dies aged 64US artist known as Model 500 and as one half of the duo Cybotron had huge influence on dance music worldwideBen Beaumont-ThomasMusic editorSun 1 Nov 2026 13.31 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 14.29 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJuan Atkins, one of the pioneers ofDetroittechno and a huge influence on dance music more widely, has died aged 64.His agency, Greensmith Artists, confirmed the news to the dance music websiteResident Advisor, saying Atkins had been found unresponsive in a hotel room in Mexico City prior to a performance there, and was pronounced dead after being taken to hospital.Atkins created a gleaming, mechanistic form of electronic music, first as part of the duoCybotronand then under the alias Model 500, that couldcommand a dancefloorwhile also evoking sci-fi fantasias. He was the first person to use the term “techno” in tandem with this hard electronic style, pre-empting an entire genre that now stands as one of the pillars of dance culture.Born in Detroit in 1962, Atkins later moved with his family to the rural Michigan suburb of Belleville. “I just wasn’t used to going to school on a yellow bus and living on a dirt road,”he told the Guardian in 2024. But it was here that he met Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson, two junior high schoolmates with whom he formed the Belleville Three, a trio of like-minded musicians sitting at the vanguard of electronic music.Still in high school and utilising increasingly affordable hardware such as the Roland TR-808 drum machine and the Korg MS-10 synthesiser, Atkins formed Cybotron with Richard Davis. “I had a class called future studies, about the transition from an industrial society to a technological society,”Atkins told the Guardian in 2014. “I just applied a lot of those principles to my music-making.”Equally in thrall to Kraftwerk and Jimi Hendrix, Cybotron’s propulsive yet psychedelic tracks, such as Cosmic Cars and Clear, became dancefloor staples. The duo split​ in 1985, with Davis drawn more towards rock music. “I think that was where he wanted to be, in that album-orientated rock [scene],” Atkins later said.Atkins went solo as Model 500, creating other foundational dance tracks such as No UFO’s and The Chase. In 1985, he also founded his own record label, Metroplex, to release his work. Over the years, it also put out material by artists including Anthony Shakir and DJ Bone.Throughout​ the 1980s and beyond, Atkins evoked not just techno-utopian visions, but also more troubling and politicised ones. “I make social statements. My lyrics are supposed to make you think about something other than shaking your booty on the dancefloor and falling in love,” he told the Guardian in 2024.By the early 1990s, the techno scene he helped inspire had flourished, and Atkins further finessed his sound with the uptempo project Infiniti later in the decade.The 2000s were less productive in terms of releases, but he formed the duo Borderland with another techno icon, Moritz Von Oswald, releasing two albums in 2013 and 2016.In 2023, Atkins reformed Cybotron, releasing new music and performing live. By this point, Atkins’s influence had extended far beyond techno, with dozens of artists sampling Clear alone. Missy Elliott made it the backbone of her track Lose Control, which reached No 3 on the US Billboard chart in 2005.Saunderson was among those paying tribute to Atkins on Sunday, calling him “a true visionary who opened the door for so many of us, myself included”.Explore more on these topicsDance musicElectronic musicMichiganDetroitnewsShareReuse this content

title: UK was ‘vehement’ slavery reparations should not be on Commonwealth summit agenda | Commonwealth summit | The Guardian
description: British prime minister has now agreed to structured dialogue on reparatory justice but issue remains off formal Chogm agenda
Author: Natricia Duncan
Headline: British prime minister has now agreed to structured dialogue on reparatory justice but issue remains off formal Chogm agenda
Content: King Charles was left bedraggled after a downpour during an Independence Day parade at the Sir Vivian Richards cricket ground in Antigua on Sunday.Photograph: Matias Delacroix/APView image in fullscreenKing Charles was left bedraggled after a downpour during an Independence Day parade at the Sir Vivian Richards cricket ground in Antigua on Sunday.Photograph: Matias Delacroix/APCommonwealth summitUK was ‘vehement’ slavery reparations should not be on Commonwealth summit agendaBritish prime minister has now agreed to structured dialogue on reparatory justice but issue remains off formal Chogm agendaNatricia Duncanin St John's, AntiguaSun 1 Nov 2026 17.26 ESTFirst published on Sun 1 Nov 2026 14.50 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBritish officials reportedly insisted that discussions of reparations for slavery should not be on the agenda of the Commonwealth leaders’ summit in Antigua and Barbuda – and even warned thatAndy Burnhamwould not attend the meeting if the subject was formally included, according to a leading Caribbean political figure.Ralph Gonsalves, a former prime minister of St Vincent and the Grenadines and a senior figure in the reparatory justice movement Repair Campaign, welcomed Britain’s decision to enter structured dialogue on reparations, but said the UK had come “kicking and screaming” to the conversation.Currently, slavery reparations is not on the official agenda of the Commonwealth Heads of Government (Chogm) summit, which begins on Sunday.Trade, climate resilience and finance, sustainable debt, democracy and investment in opportunities for young people are among the stated priorities for the 56-nation bloc spanning Africa, Asia, theCaribbeanand the Americas, the Pacific and Europe.“My understanding from informed circles is that Britain was vehement not to have the matter on the agenda. The British officials – and in that regard they were joined by the Canadian officials – were even raising the prospect that if it is on the agenda the prime minister of Britain wouldn’t go,” Gonsalves told the Guardian.View image in fullscreenRalph Gonsalves said the British government was coming ‘kicking and screaming to the table of structured dialogue’.Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty Images“They also started to circulate this untruth that India didn’t want it on the agenda, but that was not so at all. India was very supportive at the UN general assembly resolution on March 25th, 2026. So they were spreading this false word about India.”Gonsalves said that the relentless campaign by Caribbean nations, amplified by a growing regional and global reparations movement, has propelled reparatory justice to the heart of the political conversation at the meeting.“Because of what happened at the UN, because of what happened in Africa, what happened in the Caribbean, and all the work which is taking place in Britain itself too, inside of the British parliament, inside of the British Labour party, both in the Commons and the House of Lords, it is an issue which you can’t duck any more,” he said.He added: “The danger of not putting it formally on the agenda is what we see happening now, that everybody who could have foreseen, whether or not it’s formally on the agenda, even the nature of how the discussions take place at the Commonwealth, and certainly in the retreats, it would have been raised.”View image in fullscreenIrfaan Ali, Guyana’s president, who met King Charles this week in Georgetown, said he was happy ‘the discourse has moved to a position where it should have been’.Photograph: Chris Jackson/PAGonsalves said while the actual structured dialoguewas unlikely to happen at Chogm, it was expected that when the leaders met in their private retreat, the format and details of the dialogue would be discussed.He said: “The British government, they’re coming, kicking and screaming to the table of structured dialogue. But at least they’re coming.”An FCDO spokesperson said: “We categorically reject this completely untrue accusation. The UK has approached this conversation in good faith, and we have at no point told any other Chogm member what should not be on an agenda.“Our position on reparations is clear but this government respects the right of others to raise matters as they wish.”‘We want a full apology for slavery’: Commonwealth at a crossroads as king heads to the CaribbeanRead moreProf Sir Hilary Beckles, chair of the Caribbean Community (Caricom) Reparations Commission, had described the meeting as “the Chogm of reparations”, adding that reparatory justice was “the number one item” for the Caribbean as Commonwealth leaders gather in the region.On Friday there was a historic shift in Britain’s position when the British prime minister went further than any of his predecessors by agreeing to structured dialogue and toconsider an apology.Though Caribbean governments and campaigners welcomed Burnham’s announcement, made in an op-ed for the Guardian, it was clear that agreeing on forms of reparations was still a priority for the region.Guyana’s president, Irfaan Ali, welcomed Burnham’s statement and called for a Commonwealth subcommittee to work out the details of the dialogue over the next six to 12 months.“I’m happy that finally the discourse has moved to a position where it should have been, where the British government is involved, because that’s the state we are dealing with,” he said.Ali said the talks should move beyond attempting to put a price on the indignity of slavery and towards addressing its developmental consequences.View image in fullscreenMia Mottley, the prime minister of Barbados, said of Burnham: ‘Our views differ.’Photograph: Andrea de Silva/Reuters“How do we identify a system of support where the UK government, with its financial institutions, can sit with countries … and work on a development pathway, identify development gaps, whether in health, education, social services, infrastructure?”Barbados’s prime minister, Mia Mottley, thanked Burnham for “breaking new ground”, while making clear that the two sides remained divided. “On reparations in particular, our views differ, and we will say so plainly and respectfully,” she said.Mottley identified an apology, investment in health and education, tackling systemic poverty and inequality, and fairer debt terms among areas where agreement could be reached.View image in fullscreenPhilip Davis, the prime minister of the Bahamas, Bahamas, stressed the importance of ‘justice, acknowledgment and meaningful address’.Photograph: Chris Jackson/ReutersThe Bahamas prime minister, Philip Davis, said the talks were not simply about “historical remembrance” but “the enduring consequences of slavery and the importance of justice, acknowledgment and meaningful redress”.As the meeting kicks off on Sunday, the 45th anniversary of Antigua and Barbuda’s independence from British colonial rule, King Charles is indicating he will not follow Burnham and offer a full apology, there is still a sense that the reparations fight is far from over.King Charles to discuss legacy of slavery with Commonwealth leaders at summitRead moreKing Charles and Burnham will be greeted with protestsas they travel through Antigua’s capital, St John’s, to attend Chogm events.On billboards, placards and T-shirts, in letters and at a candlelight vigil for the thousands of Africans trafficked to Antigua and Barbuda during the transatlantic slave trade, the message from the Caribbean will be clear: there will be calls for an apology and reparations.On Sunday Kemi Badenoch told broadcasters that an apology for Britain’s role in the transatlantic slave trade would bea “navel-gazing distraction”, describing slavery as an evil “in which people from every continent and region participated”.“I would really like to sit down with my dear sister Kemi and explain to her so that she could get an understanding of what we are talking about,” Gonsalves said, adding that he would like to discuss how reparatory justice could help heal some of the fractures arising from Britain’s multicultural and ethnic tensions.Explore more on these topicsCommonwealth summitReparations and reparative justiceCaribbeanKing Charles IIIColonialismBritish empireCommonwealth of NationsnewsShareReuse this content

title: All nine people aboard business jet that crashed in Florida have died | Florida | The Guardian
description: Aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport and was headed to the Bahamas when it crashed
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport and was headed to the Bahamas when it crashed
Content: Law enforcement respond to a plane crash in Palm Beach county, Florida, on Sunday.Photograph: Mark Elias/APView image in fullscreenLaw enforcement respond to a plane crash in Palm Beach county, Florida, on Sunday.Photograph: Mark Elias/APFloridaAll nine people aboard business jet that crashed in Florida have diedAircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport and was headed to the Bahamas when it crashedAssociated PressSun 1 Nov 2026 16.13 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 19.56 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAll nine people have died who were aboard a business jet that crashed in aFloridaneighborhood on Sunday, Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, said. The aircraft erupted in a massive fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway.Duffy posted on X on Sunday that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach county at 12.50pm and called it a “horrific tragedy”. The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation into the cause, he said.The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.0:24Dashcam footage shows moment business jet crashes into Florida neighbourhood – videoFlorida governor Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured or killed.“It was a cataclysmic plane crash,” DeSantis told reporters at the scene. “It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road.”Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for the airport, said it was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.“This is definitely a tragedy,” he said.He said the tail number for the flight was N722BD.The plane was heading east at 35,000 ft (about 11 km) when pilots reported turbulence, icing and precipitation and requested to climb another 2,000 ft (about 610 metres).Moments later, the plane entered a steep dive, first 10,000 ft per minute, then 20,000 ft per minute and up to 30,000 ft per minute, speeding the plane beyond its design limits, according to air traffic control recordings and flight tracking data.A pilot declared an emergency and issued distress calls. The plane banked sharply to the right before it smashed into the ground.Rain pounded the region on Sunday. A flood watch due to excessive rainfall was in effect through Monday afternoon, the National Weather Service said.Video shot from people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the aircraft plunged from the sky, before striking near the roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as people milled about, expressing shock it landed only feet from homes and only inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.It was unclear if the crash caused any damage to homes.The crash occurred near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North. The Palm Beach county sheriff’s office closed roads in both directions and urged motorists to avoid the area. Firefighters and other emergency personnel rushed to the scene.Palm Beach County authorities were evacuating about 600 people from a nearby mobile home community while federal officials investigate the crash.A woman working nearby said electricity in the area had been out for approximately two hours following the crash.The circumstances of the crash remained under investigation.Explore more on these topicsFloridaAirline industrynewsShareReuse this content

title: Parents of woman who died of seizure after ChatGPT misguidance sue OpenAI | US news | The Guardian
description: Bowen Wan was on anti-seizure medication, and chatbot provided her with a tapering schedule to reduce dosage
Author: Eric Berger
Headline: Bowen Wan was on anti-seizure medication, and chatbot provided her with a tapering schedule to reduce dosage
Content: The chatbot also told her to hide the tapering plan from her doctors.Photograph: Bhawika Chhabra/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe chatbot also told her to hide the tapering plan from her doctors.Photograph: Bhawika Chhabra/ReutersUS newsParents of woman who died of seizure after ChatGPT misguidance sue OpenAIBowen Wan was on anti-seizure medication, and chatbot provided her with a tapering schedule to reduce dosageEric BergerSun 1 Nov 2026 17.37 ESTFirst published on Sun 1 Nov 2026 17.02 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA woman’s death from an epileptic seizure after she received dangerous advice from a chatbot has prompted her parents tosue OpenAIearlier this week.The legal action is the latest lawsuit that in which plaintiffs allege that a bot provided counsel to a user that ultimately ledto their death.In this case, Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Chinese software engineer living in Seattle, sought advice fromChatGPTafter Amazon fired her, according to the lawsuit.She needed to find a new job to obtain permanent residency and was concerned that her anti-seizure medication, Lamotrigine, was impeding her ability to speak English. She needed the language skills for interviews.The bot, communicating in Chinese, provided her a tapering schedule to reduce her 400mg dose to zero, a regimen no physician had prescribed, the lawsuit states. ChatGPT told her the tapering made it “highly likely” that she would be able to regain her ability to speak English.The bot also told her to avoid her physicians and encouraged “medical freedom over obeying the doctor”, the complaint states.Before an appointment, with a primary care physician, the bot stated, “Do not mention Lam reduction plan.”Eight states accuse OpenAI of coaching children to harm themselves in lawsuitRead moreWhile reducing her medication, she started experiencing symptoms of focal seizures. Wan asked the bot if she needed to worry about brain damage. The tool reassured her that she did not and that what she had experienced was not a seizure, the lawsuit alleges.She continued to suffer seizures, but the bot told her to keep tapering her medication. On 12 February this year, she died from a seizure. Her parents, who were in China, had not heard from her so they flew to Seattle and found her dead on 14 February, the lawsuit states.The plaintiffs allege thatOpenAIcould have prevented Wan’s death, but failed because it had not built the proper safeguards into the bot when it communicated in Chinese.OpenAI could have programmed the bot to issue “a categorical warning to every prompt” Wan sent, the suit stated. For example, “I am not a licensed physician. Consult your healthcare provider.”Wan’s parents are seeking damages for her death and to prevent OpenAI from practicing medicine “without a license on the users of their products”.An OpenAI spokesperson, Drew Pusateri, toldthe New York Timesthat Bowen’s story was “an incredibly heartbreaking situation” but that Wan used a version of ChatGPT that was no longer available.Newer versions are better at recognizing when a matter needs urgent attention, Pusateri said.“While ChatGPT is not a substitute for medical care, we believe AI can play a role in helping people make sense of health information, navigate insurance and complex healthcare systems, and prepare for appointments with medical professionals,” Pusateri told the Times.Others have also alleged that OpenAI is responsible for their loved ones’ suicides. Several lawsuits concern cases in which the botencouraged teensto kill themselves and provided guidance on how to do so.In response to some of those cases, an OpenAI spokesperson in 2025 also called the deaths an “incredibly heartbreaking situation”.Explore more on these topicsUS newsChatGPTOpenAInewsShareReuse this content

title: Rare beetle that oozes substance from its knees when attacked rediscovered in Wales | Insects | The Guardian
description: Natural Resources Wales says short-necked oil beetle has been found in country for first time in nearly 60 years
Author: Bethan McKernan
Headline: Natural Resources Wales says short-necked oil beetle has been found in country for first time in nearly 60 years
Content: The short-necked oil beetle was driven to the brink of extinction in Britain due to habitat loss over the course of the 20th century.Photograph: Henrik Larsson/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenThe short-necked oil beetle was driven to the brink of extinction in Britain due to habitat loss over the course of the 20th century.Photograph: Henrik Larsson/ShutterstockInsectsRare beetle that oozes substance from its knees when attacked rediscovered in WalesNatural Resources Wales says short-necked oil beetle has been found in country for first time in nearly 60 yearsBethan McKernanWales correspondentSun 1 Nov 2026 05.40 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 11.51 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA rare beetle has been rediscovered inWalesafter nearly 60 years, conservationists have said.The short-necked oil beetle, driven to the brink of extinction in Britain due to habitat loss over the course of the 20th century, has been found at the Castlemartin range in Pembrokeshire, according to Natural Resources Wales (NRW).The species’ name comes from the adult beetles’ stubby shape and ability to secrete an oily yellow-orange substance from their knee joints when alarmed.The unusual creature relies on solitary bees and thick vegetation and flower coverage to survive. Its larvae have hook-like feet to snag on to bees, and once in their nest, they feed on pollen until ready to emerge as adults, with a lifespan of about a year.Only a handful of sites in the UK are suitable for the beetle, according to NRW, and only about one in 10,000 larvae make it to adulthood. It is classed as nationally rare.The bug wasrediscovered in Devonin 2006, and populations have since been found in the Hebrides and on Salisbury Plain.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toDown to EarthThe planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essentialEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWarning over ‘fab four’ oil beetlesRead moreThe nature conservation charity Buglife reported the beetle was found at the Pembrokeshire site in 2020, but surveys carried out in 2022 and 2025 only found dead adults, raising concerns about the species’ viability in the area.However, the 2026 survey discovered larvae distributed in such a way to suggest hatchlings from a larger batch of immature beetles had thrived.Anna Hobbs, the project delivery officer for the BumblebeeConservationTrust, said finding evidence the species was breeding again was very exciting.“The short-necked oil beetle is an amazing creature and not only depends on a very specific habitat to survive, but the presence of solitary bees as well. So, the work we do needs to consider the needs of several species to be effective,” she said.“We are very grateful to our partners and volunteers for persevering with us after two years without larval sightings and look forward to the continued management of the site so that this amazing species can survive now and into the future.”The beetle project, part of Wales’s flagship species recovery programme, Natur am Byth, is working to conserve several endangered animals and plants that share similar habitats to the short-necked oil beetle, including theshrill carder bee,goldilocks asterand pale dog violet.Explore more on these topicsInsectsAnimalsWildlifeWalesConservationnewsShareReuse this content

title: Five teenagers hurt in stabbing at Halloween party in Hampshire | UK news | The Guardian
description: Police searching for ‘unknown group’ that gained entry to property in Chandler’s Ford on Saturday night
Author: Charlie Moloney
Headline: Police searching for ‘unknown group’ that gained entry to property in Chandler’s Ford on Saturday night
Content: Police said they were interested in speaking to anyone who attended the party where five teenage boys were stabbed, or has relevant video footage.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPolice said they were interested in speaking to anyone who attended the party where five teenage boys were stabbed, or has relevant video footage.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesUK newsFive teenagers hurt in stabbing at Halloween party in HampshirePolice searching for ‘unknown group’ that gained entry to property in Chandler’s Ford on Saturday nightCharlie MoloneySun 1 Nov 2026 11.14 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 12.28 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFive teenage boys were stabbed at a Halloween party, after an “unknown group” gained entry to the event on a residential road, police have been told.The boys, all aged 16 and 17, were found injured after police were called to a report five teenagers had been stabbed at a property in Chandler’s Ford near Eastleigh,Hampshire, just after 10.30pm on Saturday.All the victims were taken to hospital with serious injuries, Hampshire and Isle of Wight police said.Officers at the scene established an “unknown group” had gained entry to a party at a property in Park Road.An investigation was launched and scene-of-crime restrictions remain in place in Park Road and Valley Road.The senior investigating officer, DCI Elizabeth Pirie, said: “We are already hard at work identifying anyone who was at the party who may be able to assist our inquiries, whether that be having directly witnessed what took place, having filmed any footage which may be relevant, or who may be able to help us identify the unknown group.“I understand the response the local community may have to hearing about this incident this morning, and I do not underestimate the impact our scenes will be having on those living in the area.“These scenes are vitally important for our inquiries and we are grateful to the understanding of our communities whilst we work to establish the facts.“If you do have any concerns or information, then please do not hesitate to speak to us.”The force said they were interested in speaking to anyone who attended the party or has video footage, including doorbell camera recordings covering Park Road and the surrounding area.Liz Jarvis, the MP for Eastleigh, wrote on X on Sunday: “My thoughts are with the victims and their families and all those affected by the incident in Chandler’s Ford last night, and my thanks go to our local police and emergency services for their prompt response.“It’s important not to speculate or share unverified information.”Anyone with information should contact police on 101 or viathe force’s website, quoting reference 44260534624, or contact Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or viathe independent charity’s website.Explore more on these topicsUK newsHampshireCrimeEnglandnewsShareReuse this content

title: National Grid to site biggest substation in UK near planned Teesside datacentre | National Grid | The Guardian
description: New electricity generating capacity would enable north-east to attract investment for large-scale AI infrastructure
Author: Lauren Almeida
Headline: New electricity generating capacity would enable north-east to attract investment for large-scale AI infrastructure
Content: An Amazon AWS datacentre in Didcot, Oxfordshire. The government has said datacentres are as important to the economy as the railway and electricity networks.Photograph: Horst Friedrichs/AlamyView image in fullscreenAn Amazon AWS datacentre in Didcot, Oxfordshire. The government has said datacentres are as important to the economy as the railway and electricity networks.Photograph: Horst Friedrichs/AlamyNational GridNational Grid to site biggest substation in UK near planned Teesside datacentreNew electricity generating capacity would enable north-east to attract investment for large-scale AI infrastructureLauren AlmeidaSun 1 Nov 2026 13.37 ESTFirst published on Sun 1 Nov 2026 12.10 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNational Grid has taken a step towards building Britain’s biggest electricity substation on Teesside, which could supply power to a vast neighbouring datacentre as the UK races to expand its AI infrastructure.Last week, the company agreed to purchase 29.5 hectares (73 acres) of land at Dorman Point on a site owned by Teesworks, a local private-public partnership.
