Content: Kai Havertz scores what proved to be Arsenal’s winner against Liverpool.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersView image in fullscreenKai Havertz scores what proved to be Arsenal’s winner against Liverpool.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersPremier LeagueArsenal hold on for first league win at Liverpool since 2012 after Kai Havertz pounces earlyDavid Hytnerat AnfieldSun 1 Nov 2026 13.44 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 17.04 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt was a game when Arsenal showed their ruthless side and all of the champion knowhow that they accumulated over the course of last season. They headed back to London having made a statement. Irrespective of what happens to Manchester City over their financial rule breaches, Arsenal remain the Premier League’s team to beat.Mikel Arteta was in the Arsenal midfield when the clublast won a league fixture at Anfield; it was in September 2012, although his memories are a little hazy given the concussion that he sustained in a collision with Jordan Henderson.‘We have to tell them to go down’: Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial for LiverpoolRead moreArteta has a clear-eyed focus on retaining the title and this was an occasion for his hopes to surge. Kai Havertz’s first goal in 10 appearances proved the difference but the victory was rooted in Arsenal’s capacity to control and frustrate.It was a tough watch for theLiverpoolcrowd and they bayed throughout at what they perceived as Arsenal’s use of the dark arts. Arteta’s team won 18 free-kicks and there were some soft ones – each was the prompt for an eruption from the Kop. It said plenty that Virgil van Dijk responded to the full-time whistle by sarcastically applauding the referee, Andy Madley. The Liverpool captain was booked.The home team had their grievances. Alexander Isak felt Jurriën Timber grab a handful of his shirt in the 21st minute as he tried to reach a Bradley Barcola cross in front of goal. It was a mystery as to why the video assistant referee did not alert Madley. Van Dijk could also be heard shouting in the tunnel afterwards at Noni Madueke, saying the Arsenal winger should have had a second yellow card.Madueke, who was booked for a foul on Barcola, took a risk when he initiated a touch of foreheads with Alexis Mac Allister towards the end after a melee had broken out. It was sparked by Mac Allister’s furious reaction to Martin Ødegaard’s winning of a free-kick. Liverpool, however, lost any claim to the moral high ground when Mac Allister crumpled to the turf in an attempt to get Madueke sent off. The Arsenal player survived. It would have been a harsh dismissal.View image in fullscreenAlexis Mac Allister clashes with Jurriën Timber as tempers flare.Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty ImagesIn the final analysis, Liverpool did not do enough. They provided high‑energy enjoyment in the first half but they fizzled out, the invention drying up. They finished with no shots on target as their five-match winning run in all competitions ground to a halt. Goals remain a problem for them in the league and the truth was Arsenal kept them out with a measure of comfort. Arsenal’s previous trip to the north‑west had ended inCarabao Cup humiliation at Fleetwoodon Tuesday night. This was much more like it.Liverpool brought the intensity at the outset with Trey Nyoni snapping into challenges on his full league debut. The 19-year-old’s first action was to leave something on Ødegaard and, not long after that, he did the same to Havertz. Nyoni was fortunate to emerge without a yellow card.The tone was set early, the Kop teeming with indignation at what they saw as Arsenal’s readiness to go down easily and stay down. The match was shaped by Havertz’s goal on 16 minutes and from a Liverpool point of view, it was a self-inflicted wound. Alisson tried to be too cute with a short pass out from his area for Jérémy Jacquet; the weight and direction of it was wrong. But when Ødegaard pounced, a stunning piece of interplay followed. Arsenal worked it over and up the right for Declan Rice to flash over the final ball, low and across the corridor of a six-yard box of uncertainty. Havertz, a player who needed an easy tap-in, got one.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLiverpool’s work in progress fizzles out in the face of streetwise champions | Andy HunterRead moreLiverpool responded with more fire and they could have scored before the interval, Mac Allister blowing the big chance – a free header from Milos Kerkez’s cross in the 43rd minute. Moments earlier, Florian Wirtz had whipped a free-kick from the left‑hand side against the crossbar.Arsenal flickered on the break. There were a few times in the first half when they flooded men forward and there were possibilities. This was a long way from being a smash‑and‑grab. Havertz narrowly failed to get a touch to a Bruno Guimarães cross-cum-shot while Timber could not react in front of goal after Madueke volleyed a Christos Tzolis cross back from an acute angle.Arsenal had the match where they wanted it. They backed themselves to keep Liverpool at bay. It was about their game management. They have become masters at drawing the sting and the longer the second half went on the more assured Arsenal looked. They stifled Liverpool and there remained the sense they could land something on the counter.When Jacquet slipped in the 68th minute, Arsenal went left to Tzolis and he almost teed up Ødegaard. With Alisson out of position, Jacquet got back to make an important intervention. Tzolis also forced an excellent save with a first‑time shot for the far corner. Liverpool fought a losing battle to keep a lid on their emotions. They huffed and they puffed. The equaliser never looked like coming.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueLiverpoolArsenalmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: New York City Marathon: Andreas Almgren wins on debut as Sheila Chepkirui reclaims crown | New York City Marathon | The Guardian
description: Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women’s race for the second time, while Sweden’s Andreas Almgren claimed the men’s title in his first race over the distance
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women’s race for the second time, while Sweden’s Andreas Almgren claimed the men’s title in his first race over the distance
Content: Sweden's Andreas Almgren and Kenya's Sheila Chepkirui celebrate their victories.Photograph: Jeenah Moon/ReutersView image in fullscreenSweden's Andreas Almgren and Kenya's Sheila Chepkirui celebrate their victories.Photograph: Jeenah Moon/ReutersNew York City MarathonNew York City Marathon: Andreas Almgren wins on debut as Sheila Chepkirui reclaims crownKenya’s Sheila Chepkirui wins second women’s titleUSA’s Jessica Jessica McClain finishes in secondSweden’s Andreas Almgren wins men’s race on debutGuardian sportand agenciesSun 1 Nov 2026 11.33 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 14.27 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women’s race of theNew York City Marathonon Sunday for the second time, while Sweden’s Andreas Almgren claimed the men’s title in his first ever race over the distance.Almgren was making his debut at 26.2 miles after a successful career running half marathons and the 10,000m. He pulled away from Yemaneberhan Crippa of Italy in the final mile to take the victory in two hours, six minutes and one second. Crippa finished 13 seconds behind. Kamohelo Mofolo of Lesotho was third, edging out defending champion Benson Kipruto.“I’ve probably never felt so emotional after a race ever,” said Almgren. “With 5k left I felt like I had the legs today … I saw I had a pretty big gap [near the end of the race] and thought: ‘OK, just enjoy these last few hundred meters’, because this is not something a lot of people get to experience.”Almgren looked to be a veteran over the ⁠distance as he hung in with a crowded lead pack ​through the demanding ​and hilly course. He pulled away ​from the defending champion Kipruto with one mile ​left and had ‌built such a ​comfortable lead by ​the final meters that he jogged across the line, waving his arms as he coaxed more cheers from the crowd.“This is my first marathon. I didn’t know how I was supposed to feel,” said Almgren.Chepkirui, who also won the race in 2024, pulled away from her compatriot Hellen Obiri in the final 150m to seal the victory in 2:24.36.“The last mile was really tricky, I knew I had to be patient because Hellen was really strong so I had to really push up to the finish line,” said Chepkirui. “I am so happy.”American Jessica McClain finished second in the women’s race, passing Obiri – a two-time winner – in the final few strides. It was the first time a US woman has finished in the top three since 2018. McClain was six seconds behind Chepkirui.“It was a really fun, magical day out there,” said McClain. “I really didn’t feel great through 18 miles. I just had to stick with it. I don’t really know what happened but I couldn’t be happier right now.”Marcel Hug won the men’s wheelchair race for the eighth time, edging Daniel Romanchuk by just over a second. Romanchuk made a move to take over the lead in the last mile as the pair entered Central Park for the final time. Hug passed him in the final stretch to win.Catherine Debrunner pulled away from the field early to win the women’s wheelchair race, finishing in 1:40:02. It was the second-fastest time in race history, trailing her own mark by about 30 seconds from 2023. Two-time defending champion Susannah Scaroni finished third, three months after giving birth to her first child, more than eight minutes behind Debrunner.It was the 50th time that the race has run through all five boroughs of the city. There were just over 2,000 competitors in the seventh running of the race, including just 88 women. About 60,000 runners stepped up to the starting line Sunday, with nearly half of them women.Explore more on these topicsNew York City MarathonMarathonAthleticsUS sportsNew YorknewsShareReuse this content

title: Ciara Mageean, European 1500m gold medallist with Ireland, dies aged 34 | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Ireland’s European 1500 metres gold medallist Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Ireland’s European 1500 metres gold medallist Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34
Content: Ciara Mageean, pictured in Glasgow in 2019, competed at the 2016 and 2020 Olympic Games and was ‘respected and loved by many people’.Photograph: Jane Barlow/PAView image in fullscreenCiara Mageean, pictured in Glasgow in 2019, competed at the 2016 and 2020 Olympic Games and was ‘respected and loved by many people’.Photograph: Jane Barlow/PAAthleticsCiara Mageean, European 1500m gold medallist with Ireland, dies aged 34Mageean won 2024 European 1500m title in RomeAthlete described as ‘an inspiration to so many’Press AssociationSun 1 Nov 2026 07.31 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 17.40 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Irish middle-distance runner Ciara Mageean, who won European gold and competed at two Olympic Games, has died aged 34, her family have announced.The athlete, from Portaferry in Northern Ireland, died at 6.30am on Sunday. In a post on social media, her family said she was surrounded by her loved ones, adding: “A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed.”Mageean was one of the most high‑profile athletes in Ireland, specialising in the 1500m event. She represented Ireland at the 2016 Rio Olympics and 2020 Tokyo Games, as well as holding a slew of Irish records.She became the first individual Irish European champion since Sonia O’Sullivan when she won gold at the 2024 championships in Rome. Mageean was unable to compete at the 2024 Olympics because of an achilles injury. The following year, she announced she had been diagnosed with cancer. She went on to marry her partner, Thomas Moran, in October only weeks before her death.Micheál Martin, the Taoiseach, said he was deeply saddened at her passing. “My heartfelt sympathies go to her husband Thomas, all her family and friends,” he said. The Tánaiste, Simon Harris, described the news as heartbreaking. He said: “She was a European champion, two-time Olympian, a proud Irish athlete and an extraordinary person.”Northern Ireland’s first minister, Michelle O’Neill, said Mageean demonstrated “extraordinary talent, determination and dedication”, adding: “I am deeply saddened to hear of the passing of Ciara Mageean, and I want to extend my heartfelt condolences to her husband Tommy, her parents, family, friends and everyone who loved her.“Ciara’s achievements in athletics brought immense pride to her local community and to people right across Ireland. From representing Ireland at two Olympic Games to winning European championship gold in Rome in 2024, Ciara demonstrated extraordinary talent, determination and dedication.View image in fullscreenCiara Mageean (left) competing for Northern Ireland at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA“However, beyond the medals, records and sporting accolades, Ciara will be remembered for her warmth, courage and tremendous strength of character. Throughout her illness, she showed a remarkable spirit and an incredible ability to find hope and joy in life, even in the most difficult circumstances. Her courage touched countless people and will leave a lasting legacy.“For a community like Portaferry, this loss will be deeply felt. Ciara was one of our own, and the pride she brought to her community and beyond will never be forgotten. At this incredibly difficult time, I hope her family and loved ones can take some comfort from knowing just how deeply she was admired, respected and loved by so many people.”The deputy first minister, Emma Little-Pengelly, said: “I am so sorry to hear of the death of Ciara Mageean, at the age of 34 years. An outstanding athlete and ambassador for her sport, Ciara was born in Portaferry, County Down, and represented Northern Ireland and predominantly Ireland on the world stage.“Ciara had outstanding success, and was an inspiration to many. She spoke with such honesty and bravery about the health battles she subsequently faced. I know so many from right across Northern Ireland were deeply proud and inspired by Ciara. My deepest condolences to her family, teammates and friends, and her husband to whom she had so recently married.”Explore more on these topicsAthleticsnewsShareReuse this content

title: One person killed in shooting outside Magic City Classic football game in Alabama | College football | The Guardian
description: One person was killed and eight others were wounded in a mass shooting outside Legion Field after the annual Magic City Classic football game on Saturday night
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: One person was killed and eight others were wounded in a mass shooting outside Legion Field after the annual Magic City Classic football game on Saturday night
Content: One person was detained for questioning over the shooting.Photograph: Charlie Riedel/APView image in fullscreenOne person was detained for questioning over the shooting.Photograph: Charlie Riedel/APCollege footballOne person killed in shooting outside Magic City Classic football game in AlabamaEight injured in shooting outside Legion FieldAnnual game draws huge crowds to BirminghamAgenciesSun 1 Nov 2026 09.10 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOne person was killed and eight others were wounded in a mass shooting outside Legion Field after the annual Magic City Classic football game on Saturday night, police in Birmingham,Alabama, said.Michael Pickett, chief of the Birmingham Police Department, said most spectators and families had left the stadium property after the game, but the shooting happened nearby, where vendors were set up along Graymont Avenue.He said he was “very grateful that more people weren’t injured.”The circumstances of the shooting were unclear. Police spokesperson De’Rell Freeman said one person had been detained and transported to police headquarters for questioning, and “multiple weapons” had been found and secured.Alabama State and Alabama A&M are historically Black universities and archrivals whose annual meeting has been played for more than 100 years. Nearly 70,000 fans attended Saturday’s game, which Alabama A&M won 31-28. The event draws huge crowds to Birmingham every year.“Everyone knows this is the largest event we have here in the city and it’s extremely taxing on our personnel,” said Pickett. “Other leaders in law enforcement recognize that and they quickly offered up support and we are grateful for that quick response.”Explore more on these topicsCollege footballCollege sportsAlabamaGun crimeUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Michael Carrick to stay in charge of Manchester United for Roma game | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United despite their slipping to 17th after Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Chelsea
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United despite their slipping to 17th after Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Chelsea
Content: Michael Carrick looks on during Manchester United’s defeat at Chelsea, which has left his side 17th in the table.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick looks on during Manchester United’s defeat at Chelsea, which has left his side 17th in the table.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianManchester UnitedMichael Carrick to stay in charge of Manchester United for Roma gameUnited 17th in Premier League after Chelsea defeatNo change expected until international breakJamie JacksonSun 1 Nov 2026 03.49 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 13.22 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick is poised to remain in charge of Manchester United for the Champions League game against Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday despitethe 2-0 defeatat Chelsea on Saturday.United have not won in nine games and have made their poorest start to a season since 1988, but Carrick’s position is expected to be reviewed again during the international break after the next round of Premier League matches, in which United host Aston Villa next Sunday.The 45-year-old head coach came close to losing his job last Monday when Jason Wilcox and Omar ­Berrada met at the training ground to discuss his future. The director of football and the chief executive decided ­Carrick should be given a chance to turn form and results around.Carrick’s side are in 17th with seven points, above the relegation zone only on goal difference.There remains a view within the hierarchy that Carrick can still transform fortunes, with United’s travelling support still backing him at the end of the defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. After the game the head coach indicated that he expected to still be in position for the Roma match. He said: “We’ve got to move forward and win matches, it’s as simple as that.”View image in fullscreenBruno Fernandes, Manchester United’s captain, looks dejected after the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianEddie Howe is Wilcox’s preferred candidate should Carrick be sacked, with contact between the parties understood to have been made. The former Newcastle manager is open to taking up the position, subject to negotiations. He would cost about £3m in compensation to Newcastle.Julian Nagelsmann, the ­former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by ­Christopher ­Vivell, United’s director of ­recruitment, who is believed to have sounded out his fellow ­German. The pair previously worked together at RB Leipzig.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarricknewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘We have to tell them to go down’: Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial for Liverpool | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: The manager rued two dismissed penalty claims by the referee and complained ‘if you don’t go down, you don’t call it’
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: The manager rued two dismissed penalty claims by the referee and complained ‘if you don’t go down, you don’t call it’
Content: Alexander Isak misses a header as Arsenal’s Jürrien Timber pulls his shirt but Liverpool were denied a penalty.Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAlexander Isak misses a header as Arsenal’s Jürrien Timber pulls his shirt but Liverpool were denied a penalty.Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty ImagesLiverpool‘We have to tell them to go down’: Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial for LiverpoolManager rues two dismissed penalty claims by refereeIraola complains ‘if you don’t go down, you don’t call it’Andy Hunterat AnfieldSun 1 Nov 2026 16.25 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 16.28 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAndoni Iraola said he will instruct Liverpool players to go down in the box in future after Alexander Isak was denied a penalty during Arsenal’s first win at Anfield for 14 years.Liverpool were beaten byKai Havertz’s early strikeafter a poor clearance from the goalkeeper ­Alisson but had two penalty claims dismissed by the referee, Andy Madley. The first, a shirt-pull by the Arsenal defender Jurriën Timber on Isak, prevented the ­Sweden international reaching Bradley Barcola’s cross. The second, a hold by Christos ­Tzolis on Cody Gakpo, was reviewed by the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell, but rejected.Arsenal hold on for first league win at Liverpool since 2012 after Kai Havertz pounces earlyRead moreIsak stood his ground when held by Timber and Iraola claimed that counted against his team. Asked whether Isak should have collapsed in the area, theLiverpoolhead coach replied: “It’s a shame you ask me this question but, honestly, yes, we have to tell them to go down because they’re not going to call it otherwise.“And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.”Iraola accepted the reasons for ­dismissing the Gakpo penalty claim but believed they were inconsistent with the explanation for not ­awarding the Isak appeal. “I think there are two situations and they are a bit related,” he said.“The Isak one is a clear penalty. He is going to head the ball in front of the goal and they grab him where ­everyone sees the shirt. The ball just goes in front of Alex and I don’t see the reason why [it isn’t given]. ­“Probably because he doesn’t dive or he doesn’t go to the floor. It shouldn’t be a reason not to concede a penalty. The Gakpo one, I think it’s a sustained holding but I understand their argument and I think they are right when they say the ball was too long in the air and Cody wouldn’t have arrived to the ball.“But then you’re basically ­accepting that the first one is a ­penalty, no? You cannot use the ­argument in both ways differently.”Iraola’s post-match mood ­contrasted starkly with his childhood friend Mikel Arteta. The Arsenal ­manager, who claimed not to have seen the Isak incident, was elated by his team’s reaction to theirCarabao Cup exit at Fleetwoodin midweek and his first win at Anfield in charge of the Gunners.Arteta said: “It feels better as a manager [to win at Anfield] because it has been such a long time without this feeling. I am extremely proud, especially given the conditions we arrived to the game.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“The defeat against Fleetwood looks like the end of the world but then you have to pick yourself up. That is the beautiful part of this game. Four days later you have to come to Anfield, and play against this manager, this team who are in a good moment, and so I am so proud of what my team has done.”Arsenal have now won at four grounds where they did not win when securing the title last season – Anfield, Villa Park, the Stadium of Light and the City Ground.“This is a mission we didn’t complete for 14 years,” Arteta said. “There were reasons for that. Some were ­psychological, some were related to the quality we showed on the pitch, and some were decisions. We knew we had to nail all of them. We knew we would have to navigate periods where we had to suffer.”When informed that his team had denied Liverpool a shot on target in aPremier Leaguegame for the first time in 16 years, Arteta said: “I didn’t know about that stat but that is incredible. It didn’t feel like that at the time, they are a team that shoots a lot so you have to be good at denying them space and blocking shots. To do that against this team is remarkable, I would say.”Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolAndoni IraolaMikel ArtetaPremier LeagueArsenalnewsShareReuse this content

title: Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: The WSL champions Manchester City were fortunate to leave London City Lionesses with three points after Lauren Hemp secured a 2-1 win
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: The WSL champions Manchester City were fortunate to leave London City Lionesses with three points after Lauren Hemp secured a 2-1 win
Content: Lauren Hemp (left) and Khadija Shaw react after Manchester City take a 2-1 lead.Photograph: Dave Shopland/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenLauren Hemp (left) and Khadija Shaw react after Manchester City take a 2-1 lead.Photograph: Dave Shopland/ShutterstockWomen's Super LeagueHemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thrillerSuzanne WrackSun 1 Nov 2026 09.13 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 12.54 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGoals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp helped Manchester City to escape from Bromley with three points after a thrilling encounter withLondon City Lionesses. It was a statement performance from the home team, despite the defeat delivering a blow to any title ambitions they may have been quietly holding on to before kick-off.The gap between the hosts and the champions is now six points, after Hemp restored City’s lead following Jana Fernández’s equaliser. But that London City had even played their way into conversations about this season’s title contenders in their second season has been impressive.Russo spares Arsenal blushes but latest setback increases pressure on SlegersRead moreAndrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City manager, praised the ability of his team to win in different ways as needed, after three games in eight days. “We said afterwards, the players should be so proud of what they put into this game,” he said.“We’ve learned we’re a great team who can keep the ball for 75% of the game and win that way, or we can win like this. That quality to win in different ways is good to have, but the players also have to adapt to that and feel it’s OK to not have the ball all the time, take pride in defending and only having three or four chances but finishing off those chances.”Before kick-off, cameras showed London City’s superstar summer signing Alexia Putellas opening the boot of her car and taking out a heavy leather-clad square item, her third Ballon d’Or safely encased inside. The Spain midfielder did not present her trophy to fans in the stands before kick-off, instead choosing to put it on display so supporters could queue to have their photo taken with it.The only nod to the player’s stunning individual year, in which she won the quadruple with Barcelona before joining London City, was on her feet, the geometric gold on her custom Ballon d’Or-themed boots glinting on their first outing.There have been jokes aplenty about the unlikelihood of the world’s premier individual award heading to its new Bromley home. To reach the stadium from Hayes Lane, you pass a field of horses on your left. London City Lionesses are not Barcelona, and they have become the home of the Ballon d’Or winner by default rather than being the key component of that individual success.Except, based on the season London City are having and the ruthless ambitions of the owner, Michelle Kang, the idea that the club could produce a season that delivers them collective success and individual success off the back of it feels less distant than it did just a few short months ago.Against the champions, London City more than held their own, the opportunity to move level on points with their opponents and league leaders Chelsea an inviting incentive. Their threat was evident within 30 seconds, when the Manchester City defender Rebecca Knaak was forced to turn Lucía Corrales’s cross wide of the far post just ahead of a waiting Isobel Goodwin.Neither team has impressed defensively this season, each only managing to keep one clean sheet in the Women’s Super League, and it made for a thrilling encounter, the high lines and aggressiveness of both attacks delivering a showstopper.Making her first WSL start for the home team, with Elene Lete hitherto preferred, Mary Earps made a huge statement with an impressive double save from a Knaak header to keep the game goalless going into the break.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenMary Earps dives at the feet of Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesCity broke the deadlock despite London City dominating and it was their most influential player who delivered. Hemp flicked the ball into the run of Shaw and with her first touch, she took it past Earps before she switched the ball on to her right foot and fired in to become just the third player to score in eight consecutive WSL starts.A deserved equaliser arrived in the 72nd minute, when Fernández was at the near post to meet a corner and her assured header sent the ball looping in at the back post.The celebrations were emphatic but they were short-lived. This is a new, more resilient Manchester City, one that survived various scares last term to secure a second WSL title, and they re-established their lead two minutes later, when Hemp stretched out a leg to poke in Mary Fowler’s cross from the right to secure the win.That London City could feel aggrieved at having not taken something from the game was a testament to their performance and how quickly progress is being made. The home team had 23 shots to City’s seven and 52 touches in the opposition box to City’s 13, but critically the visiting team were clinical when it mattered. Converting two of their three efforts on target and showing the edge needed to battle at the top.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueLondon City LionessesManchester City WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: WSL roundup: Arsenal stall despite Russo strike; Chelsea’s James suffers injury | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Arsenal salvaged a late 1-1 draw at home against Aston Villa after Chasity Grant had fired visitors ahead midway through the first half
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Arsenal salvaged a late 1-1 draw at home against Aston Villa after Chasity Grant had fired visitors ahead midway through the first half
Content: Alessia Russo wheels away after striking late to deny Aston Villa an upset at the Emirates Stadium.Photograph: Leila Coker/WSL Football/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAlessia Russo wheels away after striking late to deny Aston Villa an upset at the Emirates Stadium.Photograph: Leila Coker/WSL Football/Getty ImagesWomen's Super LeagueWSL roundup: Arsenal stall despite Russo strike; Chelsea’s James suffers injuryArsenal salvage late 1-1 draw at home against Aston VillaChelsea beat Charlton 6-0 but England ace goes off earlySuzanne WrackSun 1 Nov 2026 15.17 ESTFirst published on Sun 1 Nov 2026 10.08 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOne shot, on target and in the back of the net, was all it took for Aston Villa to reopen the wound that Arsenal had been carefully trying to stitch back up.Despite almost 65% possession, 28 shots to one, and 56 touches in the opposition box to four, Alessia Russo’s 85th-minute goal meant Arsenal were only able to salvage a point against Villa after back-to-back wins in the league and Champions League had appeared to have kickstarted their season.Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thrillerRead moreThe worst possible scenario for a team that has struggled against low blocks arrived in the 25th minute, when Lynn Wilms found Chasity Grant, who fired low into the bottom corner. It was a hammer blow to the home team, with Villa knowing exactly what to do next: stick 11 players behind the ball and frustrate the Gunners.Russo’s late goal spared Arsenal’s blushes a little, the forward flicking a header in at the far post from a Stina Blackstenius cross, but the reprieve delivered by Arsenal’s victories over Tottenham and Benfica has been rolled back.The Gunners have an incredibly tricky run of fixtures coming up, with Liverpool away followed by Barcelona, London City and then Lyonnes. And, despite the back-to-back wins, they haven’t been able to resolve the problems in the final third that have plagued every performance.The pressure will be back on head coach Renée Slegers and there are questions to be asked about some decision making. However, with similar problems present under Joe Montemurro and Jonas Eidevall before her, maybe it’s time to look beyond the head coach.Elsewhere Lauren James was forced off with an injury in the first half ofChelsea’s 6-0 win atCharlton. The England forward was replaced by Erin Cuthbert in the 35th minute with the away team 4-0 up. There were five different goalscorers with Melvine Malard getting two. The coach, Sonia Bompastor, said: “It is too soon [to know] about Lauren’s injury. I spoke to her at half-time and it seems to be her hamstring so we will have to have a proper assessment tomorrow.”Tottenhamclimbed to fourth in the table after a comprehensive 4-1 win atBirmingham City. The Spurs midfielder Drew Spence set a new all-time WSL appearance record with 2017 to move one above the former Chelsea defender Millie Bright.West Hamwere also 4-1 winners, overLiverpool, in their third league win of the season, leapfrogging their opponents in the table to move up to 10th.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAnnabel Blanchard gaveCrystal Palacethe lead atBrightonwith a glorious long-range effort but the visitors could not hold on and strikes from Caitlin Hayes and Sophie Peskett completed the turnaround 2-1 win for Arturo Ruiz’s side. “I think that these three wins in a row will be key for the rest of the season and we are in a very good moment,” Ruiz told the club website. “And I think that we are showing what we want to do in terms of our energy. The first half was very good even though we conceded a goal.”Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueArsenal WomenAston Villa WomenBirmingham City WomenTottenham Hotspur WomenBrighton & Hove Albion WomenCrystal Palace WomennewsShareReuse this content

Author: Guardian staff reporter

title: Scottish roundup: Falkirk shock Celtic; Hibernian beat Hearts in semi-final | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Celtic slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership while Hibernian will face Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup final after defeating Hearts 2-1
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Celtic slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership while Hibernian will face Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup final after defeating Hearts 2-1
Content: Ethan Ross and Scott Bain of Falkirk enjoy the 2-0 victory over Celtic.Photograph: Mark Runnacles/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenEthan Ross and Scott Bain of Falkirk enjoy the 2-0 victory over Celtic.Photograph: Mark Runnacles/ShutterstockScottish PremiershipScottish roundup: Falkirk shock Celtic; Hibernian beat Hearts in semi-finalPressure on Martin O’Neill after 2-0 defeat by FalkirkHibs will face Rangers in Premier Sports Cup finalPress AssociationSun 1 Nov 2026 12.28 ESTFirst published on Sat 31 Oct 2026 16.36 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCelticslumped to a 2-0 defeat atFalkirkon Sunday to ramp up the scrutiny on manager Martin O’Neill after a run of three wins in 10 games. The Scottish champions had the chance to extend their lead at the top of the table to seven points, but never recovered from conceding a third-minute opener to Ethan Ross.Scott Tanser scored a second before half-time and the Bairns even had a third goal ruled out by a video assistant referee review for handball against Jacob Murrell. The majority of Celtic’s struggles this season have come in European competition as they crashed out of theChampions League qualifiersand have lost all three Europa League group matches.But sloppy defensive errors and a lack of a clear tactical plan are beginning to cost them domestically as well.Rangerscould now close to within one point of their Old Firm rivals should they win a game in hand.“We’re still in a decent position at this minute,” said a defiant O’Neill. “I keep out the noise at the end of it all. A tough one to take because I know we conceded two goals but we could have scored six or seven dead easily.”Falkirk had not beatenCelticsince March 2007, but were well worthy of a fourth consecutive victory to move up to fourth in the table. O’Neill recalled Cameron Carter-Vickers to the heart of his defence, but that decision backfired when the American international presented the ball to Ross to slam home the opening goal.Quick GuideScottish Premiership roundup: Saints dedicate draw to dismissed StewardShowSimo Valakari dedicatedSt Johnstone’s battling 2-2 draw atKilmarnockto the goalkeeper Toby Steward, who was dismissed in the 14th minute (pictured) after misjudging a long ball and handling outside his penalty area. Saints then twice fell behind to Cathal McCarthy and Djenairo Daniels, but equalised both times with goals from Danny Schmidt and Joel Cotterill to capture an unlikely point. The substitute goalkeeper Ross Sinclair, who came on at the expense of Taylor Steven, also made multiple second-half saves to help Saints move up to seventh.Valakari, the St Johnstone manager, said: “Toby has held his hands up and said: ‘I am sorry, boys, for what I did.’ But our team did it for Toby, the boys did it for Taylor, who I needed to take out straight away.“We are all here playing for each other. We have got each other’s backs when things happen. That tells me my players are ready to accept any responsibility. Early red card, with Toby that’s my tactical choice. I ask my keeper to play very high, like a sweeper-keeper for those long balls. In those moments, for a year, Toby has been fantastic in clearing the ball, reading the ball. It’s a thin line, a little outside the box, that can happen.”Alfred Johansson admitted he was left to sweat asMotherwellbroke a seven-game winless run with a 1-0 win overSt Mirren. Lukas Fadinger rattled home a penalty eight minutes from time to relieve some pressure on the Swede as the Fir Park side climbed into eighth.Johansson was adamant his team were well worthy of a result, which brought welcome relief to both him and his players. He said: “Even more than relief, I felt good, happy, joy, determination. This group has done really well lately and I think it’s very well deserved to get the victory and have at least four points from these last two games. It’s important to build on it, the most important thing today is that we didn’t give away easy goals or big chances at all."Press AssociationPhotograph: Andy Buchanan/Shutterstock EditorialWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The former Celtic goalkeeper Scott Bain was inspired in the Falkirk goal to deny Haissem Hassan and Camilo Durán, while the Colombian forward also struck a post as the visitors pressed for an equaliser. But Celtic’s leaky defence was exposed once more on 38 minutes when Tanser raced forward from left-back and drilled low into the corner.O’Neill twice rode to Celtic’s rescue last season to take interim charge, 20 years after his first spell at the club ended. The Northern Irishman then signed a one-year deal in June.Yet murmurs of discontent among the club’s fanbase have increased in recent weeks with many now calling for a change. “I’ve managed this team now for about a year, give or take a month or two, and I’ve managed before,” said O’Neill. “We’re still top of the league. We came from a mile behind last year to win the league. A mile behind on two or three occasions as well.”Marink Reedijk secured his first win asHibernianmanager with a memorable 2-1 Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory overHeartsat Hampden.View image in fullscreenJamie McGrath wheels away after scoring Hibernian’s second goal.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAA frenetic Edinburgh derby got up and running in the fourth minute when theHeartsattacker Cláudio Braga headed in from a corner, only for Martin Boyle to deservedly level in the 19th minute with a poacher’s goal. A compelling encounter continued and the midfielder Jamie McGrath put the on-top Hibernian ahead three minutes before the interval.Although Hearts retained a threat in the second half, a stout defensive display by the Leith side means they will meet Rangers in the final at Scotland’s national stadium on Sunday 13 December. Hearts had won the four previous meetings between the teams at Hampden, in 2006, 2012, 2020 and 2022, but this was Hibs’ day.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOn Saturday, Ryan Naderi’s dramatic late strike broke downAberdeen’s stubborn resistance to earnRangersa place in the final.Aberdeen restricted Rangers to one shot on target in a low-quality first half, but Derek McInnes’s side picked up the pace after the break. Aberdeen survived relentless pressure at times but in the 83rd minute Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net for his eighth goal of the season to seal a 1-0 win at Hampden Park.The 23-year-old Naderi later tried to share the glory, saying: “It feels amazing. I’m happy, of course, happy to be the one who scores the goals, but happy for the team. I think we deserved it. We believed we could score right up until the very end and we did, and I think it’s a deserved win.”View image in fullscreenRyan Naderi: a happy man.Photograph: Jamie Johnston/Focus Images Ltd/ShutterstockIt was another close-range strike from Naderi and he joked about this proficiency from distance. The Germany-born Czechia international said: “I’ve tried to shoot twice today from outside of the box and it didn’t go well. So I went back inside the box. Maybe I should just stick to the easy ones! As I said, I’m just happy how it is right now and I’m going to try to stick to it.”Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipFalkirkCelticScottish League CupHibernianHeartsRangersnewsShareReuse this content

title: Should Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts?  | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Unusually, all clubs in the top flight have the same manager with whom they began the season – but the first sacking may not be far away
Author: Andrew Beasley
Headline: Unusually, all clubs in the top flight have the same manager with whom they began the season – but the first sacking may not be far away
Content: Oliver Glasner is under pressure at Nottingham Forest after their 2-0 defeat at Brentford left them second bottom.Photograph: Andrew Kearns/CameraSport/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenOliver Glasner is under pressure at Nottingham Forest after their 2-0 defeat at Brentford left them second bottom.Photograph: Andrew Kearns/CameraSport/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueAnalysisShould Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts?Andrew BeasleyUnusually, all clubs in the top flight have the same manager with whom they began the season – but the first sacking may not be far awaySun 1 Nov 2026 13.00 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 13.50 ESTShareNoPremier Leaguemanager has yet lost his job this season. In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change.The 2026-27 season commencing with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026 has probably contributed to the early season stability. They have to be given a chance to fashion their side as they see fit. But with roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.Liverpool v Arsenal: Premier League – liveRead moreMichael Carrick remains the favourite to be the next manager to leave his post. He is unsurprisingly followed by the managers of the clubs who occupy the relegation zone: Pierre Sage of Crystal Palace, Sunderland’s Régis Le Bris and Oliver Glasner atNottingham Forest. It seems almost inevitable that Carrick will leave soon so the more interesting analysis lies among the bottom three.Sunderland sit 20th and are predicted by Opta to finish there. However, they have had a testing start to the season. Le Bris’s side have faced five of the current top seven clubs, the joint-most along with Liverpool. The manager also has enormous reserves of goodwill after taking the club back to the Premier League and then into Europe.Chart showing the standard of opposition faced by teams in the bottom half of the Premier LeagueDespite their tough schedule, Sunderland came into the weekend within one expected point of Chelsea,Manchester Unitedand Tottenham before losing 3-1 at Coventry with the xG count 1.8 to 0.7 in their favour. It was a familiar outcome for a side that has scored 6.2 goals fewer than expected this season.With Sunderland’s next five league opponents being Chelsea, Aston Villa, Tottenham, Liverpool and Newcastle, the challenge of staying up will not immediately get easier. At least their chance‑converting woes are not as bad as those of Nottingham Forest.Their shots have been worth 14.7 expected goals, the fourth most in the division after the matches on Saturday. But not once in a game this season have the goals they scored at least equalled their xG, let alone surpassed it. It is a finishing issue, not a question of opposition goalkeepers having super-human performances against them.The analytical step above standard expected goals is xG on target (xGOT). It measures the likelihood of an on-target shot becoming a goal based on chance quality and shot placement. Forest’s xGOT this season is 7.4, little more than half of their expected goal tally.This inability to test goalkeepers severely enough explains why Glasner’s men have scored just six times. They are squandering almost one goal per game on average according to their expected goals, a significant shortfall. None of the 96 teams in Europe’s big five leagues were worse than 0.5 goals per match below xG last season, which suggests Forest’s luck should turn for the better.Chart showing Nottingham Forest’s expected goals by manager since summer 2025Is Evangelos Marinakis patient enough for that to happen? Forest’s expected goal data is much stronger for Glasner than it was under any of the four managers their owner fired last season. Whether he pays attention to such numbers is a different issue.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionGlasner hinted at a physical deficiency in the squad after defeat at Brentford. “We are outrun by the opposition in every single game. We have to change it,”he said. Distance covered data from Fotmob suggests that is not quite the case, albeit Forest have been outrun in their past five league games. Both the underlying xG data and physical statistics are worse at Glasner’s former club Crystal Palace though.Chart showing expected points and points per game in 2026-27As expected goals have a far greater bearing on future performance or results than running stats, those numbers are the greater concern. Equally, Palace’s average of 96.9 sprints per match is the fewest in the Premier League (after Saturday’s matches).The club have been through similar teething troubles with new managers before. Palace’s previous two appointments that occurred between seasons were Frank de Boer and Patrick Vieira. The former was sacked after only five matches in all competitions in 2017, the latter won just one of his first nine league games four years later before recovering to finish 12th.While Palace are a little wasteful in attack, they have not been as bad as Forest or Sunderland. Their defence is a much bigger problem, which is unusual as Sage’s Lens conceded the fourth fewest expected goals in Ligue 1 last season. Palace are second worst for that metric in the Premier League in 2026‑27, rock bottom if penalties are excluded. Some of that may be down to starting seven combinations of players in the back three because of injuries and Axel Disasi’s three‑match ban, but it is imperative that a manager overcomes such inevitable difficulties.Palace host Liverpool next weekend. They return after the international break with potentially winnable games against Coventry and Hull. Will those fixtures represent a good opportunity for Sage to kickstart his reign or an excellent chance for his replacement to hit the ground running? Only the chair, Steve Parish, will know the answer but Palace are the strugglers who look most in need of managerial change.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueCrystal PalaceNottingham ForestSunderlandManchester UnitedanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Boy hands himself into police after Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland match | Sunderland | The Guardian
description: A video showed the Coventry fan, 14, at the Coventry game on Saturday with a photo of Lowery, who died aged six in 2017 with rare form of cancer
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: A video showed the Coventry fan, 14, at the Coventry game on Saturday with a photo of Lowery, who died aged six in 2017 with rare form of cancer
Content: Bradley Lowery, pictured with Jermain Defoe, captured the hearts of the football world when he was diagnosed with neuroblastoma.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAView image in fullscreenBradley Lowery, pictured with Jermain Defoe, captured the hearts of the football world when he was diagnosed with neuroblastoma.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PASunderlandBoy hands himself into police after Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland matchCoventry fan, 14, had photo of Lowery at Coventry gameBradley died aged six in 2017 with rare form of cancerPress AssociationSun 1 Nov 2026 13.20 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 15.11 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA 14-year-old boy has “handed himself in” to West Midlands police after a video posted on social media appeared to show a Coventry fan taunting Sunderland with a photo of Bradley Lowery during thePremier League match on Saturday.Sunderland fan Bradley captured the hearts of the football world when he was diagnosed with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer. He died aged six in 2017.Sakamoto sparks Coventry win to keep 10-man Sunderland rock-bottomRead moreCoventry said on Sunday that they were investigating the video footage and Bradley’s mother, Gemma, issued an emotional statement through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, which raises funds and awareness to help and support children.West Midlands police said: “We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City’s Premier League match with Sunderland [on Saturday] afternoon.“A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course. We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim’s family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.”Coventry said in their earlier statement: “Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.”Gemma Lowery said her “beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate” in her statement. She posted on Instagram: “Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.“I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between.“So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?”Lowery added: “I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t, just for him to learn from this.“Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.”Explore more on these topicsSunderlandnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘He’s done an insane job’: Antonelli’s rivals unite in praise for F1’s youngest champion | Kimi Antonelli | The Guardian
description: Lando Norris said ‘People are not giving him enough credit’ after Kimi Antonelli sealed the world drivers’ title with a third placed finish in Mexico
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Lando Norris said ‘People are not giving him enough credit’ after Kimi Antonelli sealed the world drivers’ title with a third placed finish in Mexico
Content: Kimi Antonelli is held aloft by members from his Mercedes team after he clinched the world title.Photograph: Michael Potts/LAT ImagesView image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli is held aloft by members from his Mercedes team after he clinched the world title.Photograph: Michael Potts/LAT ImagesKimi Antonelli‘He’s done an insane job’: Antonelli’s rivals unite in praise for F1’s youngest championLando Norris: ‘People are not giving him enough credit’20-year-old sealed F1 title after finishing third in MexicoGiles Richardsat the Autódromo Hermanos RodríguezSun 1 Nov 2026 18.28 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 18.42 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFormula One’s leading drivers have been unstinting in their praise for the new champion, Kimi Antonelli, after the Italian driver took hisdebut title with third placeat the Mexican Grand Prix.Antonelli became the youngest world champion at 20 years old in Mexico, sharing a podium with race winner Max Verstappen and second-placed Lewis Hamilton. He has taken the title in only his second year in the sport after a remarkable season including nine wins.Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion with third place in Mexican GPRead more“It’s a special moment,” said Antonelli. “One that we’ll remember for ever.” While his race engineer, Peter Bonnington, suggested this may well be the first of many. “It’s a ­pleasure to be on the journey with you, but it’s just the first chapter,” he said.The defending champion, Lando Norris, led what were fulsome ­tributes to the driver who had taken his crown, emphasising that he felt Antonelli had been exceptional.“He’s done an insane job. I feel like people are not giving him enough credit for what he’s achieved this year,” said Norris. “He’s beaten the teammate that’s been in the sport for four times longer than him. Who was also very good and who took the battle to Lewis Hamilton.”His achievement was perhaps not appreciated, suggested Norris, because the Italian had been so good he had made it look easy.“[Yes] 100% he’s made it look like an easy year. They say he’s not had much competition or anything, but that’s because he slapped his competition,” he added. “I think he’s done an ­unbelievable job. Incredible, incredible job.”Verstappen and Hamilton lifted Antonelli on to their shoulders on the podium to accept the roaring approval of the crowd. The four-time and seven-time champions ­respectively were generous in their praise too.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“It’s incredible, what a season [Kimi] had,” Verstappen said. “To do that at such an age is really impressive. I’m sure this is a very emotional day with him.”Hamilton said: “A huge congratulations to Kimi and the Mercedes team, they’re all here celebrating his ­success. I’m so grateful to be in the race to witness it.”Explore more on these topicsKimi AntonelliFormula OneFormula One 2026Motor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Borthwick urges England players to improve discipline at Nations Championship | England rugby union team | The Guardian
description: The coach highlighted the need to adjust to refereeing interpretations, while Ellis Genge called the timing of ‘hip-drop’ tackle law change ‘beserk’
Author: Robert Kitson
Headline: The coach highlighted the need to adjust to refereeing interpretations, while Ellis Genge called the timing of ‘hip-drop’ tackle law change ‘beserk’
Content: England’s disciplinary record in 2026 has not been good so far with 14 yellow cards and one red.Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEngland’s disciplinary record in 2026 has not been good so far with 14 yellow cards and one red.Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty ImagesEngland rugby union teamBorthwick urges England players to improve discipline at Nations Championship‘A big breakdown challenge is coming,’ warns head coachGenge calls timing of ‘hip-drop’ tackle law change ‘beserk’Robert KitsonSun 1 Nov 2026 11.00 ESTLast modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 14.16 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSteve Borthwick is urging his England players to act smarter and recognise the vital importance of keeping 15 players on the field before a pivotal month for the national team. Borthwick’s side have been shown 14 yellow cards and one red in 2026 to date and, partly as a consequence, have lost five of their past seven Tests.Borthwick is also concerned that different refereeing interpretations in the domestic Prem are not helping England at international level, with the latest complication being a mid‑season law change preventing so-called “hip-drop” tackles. His experienced prop Ellis Genge has called the timing of the alteration “berserk” but also fully accepts England must improve their disciplinary record in their autumnNations Championshipfixtures.The Breakdown | England need to unearth World Cup core despite derby friction and injury chaosRead moreAll national coaches were invited to a meeting with officials on Sunday to discover how exactly the November games will be refereed but Borthwick has already identified two key areas where England need to be watchful. “From my point of view there are some aspects we need to bridge from club rugby to Test rugby,” he said.“One would be the contact area. I think that was probably exemplified by last month’s Champions Cup round where the English clubs lost more ball at the breakdown than any other nation and won less back. That’s telling us straight away there’s a situation we need to bridge. When you look at the teams we are playing against in the next few weeks there is a big breakdown challenge coming.”Borthwick is also highlighting defensive steel – “We need to ensure we make it very, very difficult for the opposition to score” – which the head coach also believes is not being aided by the four-try bonus-point system in the Prem. He would prefer the adoption of the French system where teams must score three tries more than their opponents to secure an extra point.“My view on the bonus-point structure is that it shouldn’t be the way it is,” he said. “I think the evidence says it should follow the Top 14, which makes defence important right until the 80th minute. I think that’s not necessarily always the case [in the Prem]. Nobody’s to blame or at fault, that’s just the way it’s structured.”View image in fullscreenEllis Genge (third right) has been critical of the mid-season law change regarding ‘hip-drop’ tackles in the Prem.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianAs for his side’s tactical discipline, Borthwick has also changed his tune since July when he dubbed the media “the negativity committee” after the31-24 win against Argentinain Santiago del Estero when he was asked about England’s concession of four yellow cards in the second half. “The best players are smart and the best players adjust,” said Borthwick, who invited the referee Christophe Ridley to address his players last week.“It’s pretty obvious there have been times over the last six to eight months when we haven’t dealt with moments the way we want to. At the 2023 World Cup this team had excellent habits … really it’s been the autumn of 2025 into this year’s Six Nations that cost us.“Quite frankly we spend too much time defending. The way the interpretations are right now there is likely to be a decision that goes against you which gives an entry into the 22. As soon as you are there, we can all see the number of cards. We spent too much time there … we want to get the ball back faster.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOn the subject of outlawed “hip-drop” tackles, when players try to bring down an opponent from behind by sliding in on their knees and dropping their weight on to the opponent’s lower limbs, Borthwick also wants his players to learn fast before the game against Australia on Sunday. “I don’t think we can argue against anything that protects the players who play this intense game. What we’ve got to be is the quickest team to adjust.”Genge believes the sport as a whole needs to stop altering its regulations for the sake of the players and new fans. “I think the fact our game after all this time still changes rules year to year is berserk, particularly when we’re speaking about making it palatable for new people to come in. I think it’s mental but I assume they’re trying to refine it for the best.”England, meanwhile, have fresh injury concerns at scrum-half with Northampton’s Alex Mitchell (hamstring) and the uncapped Archie McParland (calf) struggling. With the fly-halfFin Smith (calf) already in a race against time to face the Wallabies, the management may have to start Leicester’s Jack van Poortvliet at nine, potentially with either Marcus Smith or George Ford outside him.Explore more on these topicsEngland rugby union teamSteve BorthwickNations ChampionshipRugby unionPrem RugbynewsShareReuse this content
